new_note: AbbVie books its amortisation of acquired intangibles inside cost of sales, $7,377mm of it, which is why its 29.8% cost of sales is so far above Pfizer's 25.7% and why the same test that charged Pfizer 22% charges AbbVie nothing. The older windows would imply a credit, not a cost: 33.6% over three years and 36.3% over five, both above the model, because they carry peak Humira. new_source: derived and found to be nil: AbbVie generated $17,816mm of free cash flow on $61,160mm of revenue in FY2025, a 29.13% margin, against the 28.95% its cost of sales, SG&A and R&D leave. The two reconcile to within a fifth of a point, which is why this is zero rather than absent: the check was run and it found nothing to charge. Restated before interest: ABBV paid $3,002mm of interest inside operating cash flow over 2025, 4.91% of revenue. The free cash flow above is struck after it and the valuation already charges the debt by subtracting net debt, so adding it back only widens a gap the filed lines already leave, and the charge stays nil. Restated at replacement capex: ABBV spent $1,214mm on plant over 2025 against $762mm of plant depreciation, 0.74% of revenue above what keeps the plant running. Taken at depreciation, the charge stays nil. Checked without one-off cash: deal payments are booked under investing, so free cash flow never carried them, and no settlement or transition tax is stated for the window, so the charge stands. Restated to the amortisation floor: the filed cost lines leave a 32.46% pre-tax margin where the cash over 2025 supports 38.40%, so the charge rebuilds at -5.94%. It was held at nil, but ABBV books $7,377mm of non-cash amortisation of acquired intangibles inside cost of sales in FY2025 (0001551152-26-000008), 12.06% of revenue, so the charge takes the rebuilt figure: -5.94%. Restated without working capital build: over 2025 ABBV's cash flow statement shows receivables up $1,490mm, inventories up $234mm, payables and accrued liabilities up $951mm, a working capital build of $773mm, 1.26% of revenue. Growth ties that cash up once, not on every product for ever, so the charge falls from -5.94% to -7.35%.

new_note: AbbVie books its amortisation of acquired intangibles inside cost of sales, $7,377mm of it, which is why its 29.8% cost of sales is so far above Pfizer's 25.7% and why the same test that charged Pfizer 22% charges AbbVie nothing. The older windows would imply a credit, not a cost: 33.6% over three years and 36.3% over five, both above the model, because they carry peak Humira. A backward window cannot be used to charge a company whose margin is falling
new_source: derived and found to be nil: AbbVie generated $17,816mm of free cash flow on $61,160mm of revenue in FY2025, a 29.13% margin, against the 28.95% its cost of sales, SG&A and R&D leave. The two reconcile to within a fifth of a point, which is why this is zero rather than absent: the check was run and it found nothing to charge. Restated before interest: ABBV paid $3,002mm of interest inside operating cash flow over 2025, 4.91% of revenue. The free cash flow above is struck after it and the valuation already charges the debt by subtracting net debt, so adding it back only widens a gap the filed lines already leave, and the charge stays nil. Restated at replacement capex: ABBV spent $1,214mm on plant over 2025 against $762mm of plant depreciation, 0.74% of revenue above what keeps the plant running. Taken at depreciation, the charge stays nil. Checked without one-off cash: deal payments are booked under investing, so free cash flow never carried them, and no settlement or transition tax is stated for the window, so the charge stands. Restated to the amortisation floor: the filed cost lines leave a 32.46% pre-tax margin where the cash over 2025 supports 38.40%, so the charge rebuilds at -5.94%. It was held at nil, but ABBV books $7,377mm of non-cash amortisation of acquired intangibles inside cost of sales in FY2025 (0001551152-26-000008), 12.06% of revenue, so the charge takes the rebuilt figure: -5.94%. Restated without working capital build: over 2025 ABBV's cash flow statement shows receivables up $1,490mm, inventories up $234mm, payables and accrued liabilities up $951mm, a working capital build of $773mm, 1.26% of revenue. Growth ties that cash up once, not on every product for ever, so the charge falls from -5.94% to -7.35%.

new_source: derived and found to be nil: AbbVie generated $17,816mm of free cash flow on $61,160mm of revenue in FY2025, a 29.13% margin, against the 28.95% its cost of sales, SG&A and R&D leave. Restated at replacement capex: ABBV spent $1,214mm on plant over 2025 against $762mm of plant depreciation, 0.74% of revenue above what keeps the plant running. Restated to the amortisation floor: the filed cost lines leave a 32.46% pre-tax margin where the cash over 2025 supports 38.40%, so the charge rebuilds at -5.94%. new_note: Judgement on construction: Opdivo's Part B figure scaled by the net-to-net (ASP) ratio Amgen's own IV oncology biosimilars took in Medicare in their first full year, so that the house Part B deduction in gross_to_net_pct lands the net on the biosimilar's ASP, $61,271. It is not ABP 206's own Medicare allowed amount, which would carry an add-on on the reference's ASP. Check: Horn et al. (JCO Oncol Pract 2023;19(4):e476, doi:10.1200/OP.22.00639) find the first trastuzumab biosimilar priced 15% below the originator in 2019. The 2024 annual figure was $71,752 ($1,933,800,338 over 26,951, drug_demand), so 2025 is 3.1% higher; no inflation to the 2029 launch is applied. A beneficiary's spend covers about 0.37 of a year's labelled dose (see discontinuation_pct), so this is a price per patient treated in a year, not per full year on drug. Price erosion after launch is carried separately in net_price_decline_pct
new_source: Opdivo (nivolumab, HCPCS J9299), CMS Part B 2025 from the quarterly companion bf6a5b3b-31ee-4abb-b1ad-2607a1e7510a, row '2025 (Q1-Q4)': $1,996,916,016.40 over 26,991 beneficiaries = $73,984.51 per beneficiary. Discount: the biosimilar-to-reference ASP ratio in the first full year after Amgen launched Mvasi and Kanjinti in July 2019, from CMS Part B spending per dosage unit in 2020 (drug_demand): Mvasi $62.43 against Avastin $70.86, and Kanjinti $81.55 against Herceptin $91.78. Converted to ASP by the Part B payment rule then in force: the reference is paid at ASP + 6%, and a biosimilar at its own ASP + 6% of the reference's ASP (Social Security Act 1847A(b)(8); CMS, 'Frequently Asked Questions: Inflation Reduction Act Biosimilars Temporary Payment Increase', cms.gov/files/document/biosimilar-faqs.pdf). a maintenance biologic

Benlysta (belimumab) IV, CMS Medicare Part B 2025, from the quarterly companion bf6a5b3b (HCPCS J0490, Q1-Q4 2025): $139,883,286 over 3,881 beneficiaries = $36,043.10 per beneficiary. Dazodalibep is an IV infusion in every OASIZ arm (NCT06104124, NCT06245408), and Amgen's topline release lists infusion-related reactions, so it will be billed by the clinic under Part B. Benlysta IV is the B-cell-pathway biologic given by infusion for the neighbouring systemic autoimmune disease. Using it keeps both Sjögren's claimants in one price family. Alternative: Saphnelo Part B 2025 at $38,007.17 per beneficiary (+5.4%). The 2024 annual Benlysta Part B figure was $34,064.

Social Security Act section 1847A: Medicare Part B pays 106% of average sales price, and ASP is already net of manufacturer discounts and rebates, so the manufacturer's price is the CMS figure divided by 1.06, which is 5.66% below it

Reused from pfe_dazukibart.csv, not reopened here. Bell CF et al., Lupus Sci Med 2020;7:e000357: 26.2% of 1,879 US IV belimumab starts stopped within six months, which is 45.54% a year. This is persistence on a monthly IV biologic in a rheumatic autoimmune disease, dazodalibep's own setting.

new_source: Maciel G et al., Arthritis Care Res 2017 (doi 10.1002/acr.23173): 10.3 per 10,000 adults in Olmsted County, times 266,978,268 US adults (Census NC-EST2024, 18+)
Maciel G et al., Mayo Clin Proc 2017 (doi 10.1016/j.mayocp.2017.01.020): 5.9 per 100,000 adults a year, 2006 to 2015, times 266,978,268

Identical to ianalumab, as pool_crowding requires for pooling. Maciel 2017 (doi 10.1002/acr.23173): 16 of 106 prevalent patients had ESSDAI ≥5, matching OASIZ 301's entry criterion (ESSDAI ≥5 and anti-Ro or RF positive, NCT06104124). This is a floor, with 29.5% at diagnosis as upside. If OASIZ 303 (ESSDAI <5 with ESSPRI ≥5, NCT06245408) succeeds, model that population as a separate indication row, not a larger eligible_pct, or dazodalibep leaves the shared pool.

The same anchor as ianalumab. Saphnelo's capture of the untreated CDC SLE pool, computed with backend/capture_anchor.py from AZ's filed US revenue ($111m, $260m, $425m, $596m in 2022 to 2025) at a net $35,856 per patient-year with 45.54% stopping each year, was 1.46%, 2.77%, 4.04% and 5.42%. On the fitted curve, reproducing 5.42% in year four needs a peak of 10.45%. JUDGEMENT: multiple 0.375, half of ianalumab's 0.75, giving 0.0392. That converts 2.03% of the untreated eligible pool in dazodalibep's fourth year. Case for more: the Phase 2 placebo-adjusted ESSDAI gain was -2.2 (-6.3 vs -4.1, p=0.0167, Nature Medicine 2024, doi 10.1038/s41591-024-03009-3), about twice ianalumab's Phase 3 gain across trials. It is a new mechanism (CD40L). OASIZ 303 could add the high-symptom population, which ianalumab does not reach until 2029 or later. Case against: it arrives two years after ianalumab. It is an infusion every four weeks against a monthly self-injection. Amgen has not published the OASIZ 301 effect size. Four more mechanisms are in Sjögren's Phase 3 (nipocalimab, deucravacitinib, telitacicept, efgartigimod). This is a late entrant to a crowded class, so the multiple is low. Pool crowding: with ianalumab on indication:85, pool_crowding.solve rations no year (combined starts peak at 11.7% of the eligible pool). Counting the population once trims dazodalibep's peak starts to 0.8692 of its standalone run, because ianalumab has already drawn the pool down.
new_unit: share of the untreated pool per year

new_source: The same fit as ianalumab: a least-squares logistic on Saphnelo's CMS Medicare new starts, 2022 to 2025 (935, 1,150, 1,385, 1,626, from Part B plus Part D beneficiaries net of 54.46% persistence). k=0.31, midpoint 2.76, rmse 0.4, with one degree of freedom. It is consistent with the 9-year median in data/launch_ramp.csv. Saphnelo is also an IV biologic given every four weeks in a rheumatic autoimmune disease, the same care setting as dazodalibep.

new_note: the case for more: first in class, added on rather than swapped in, so a patient keeps a TNF inhibitor that partly works; the ACPA selection matches the mechanism; and AstraZeneca already sells Saphnelo, its lupus antibody, in the US ($596mm in FY2025, 20-F 0001104659-26-019130). The case against: Orencia's label says concurrent therapy with a TNF antagonist is not recommended because infections rose without an important gain in efficacy (openFDA label set 0836c6ac-ee37-5640-2fed-a3185a0b16eb), which an effector-null antibody has to disprove; a second biologic adds a second drug bill to the first; and the Phase 2 reads a week-12 DAS28-CRP change. 2022 is not the anchor because Sanofi reports demand for IL-6 receptor blockers rose with the tocilizumab shortage announced in mid-August 2021 (20-F 0001121404-23-000008). new_source: ANCHOR, Kevzara's measured US capture. Its US net sales were EUR 64mm in 2018, 115mm in 2019, 123mm in 2020, 135mm in 2021 and 186mm in 2022 (Sanofi 20-F 0001121404-20-000006, 0001121404-21-000004, 0001121404-22-000007, 0001121404-23-000008), converted at FRED DEXUSEU annual averages of 1.1817, 1.1194, 1.1410, 1.1830 and 1.0534. MULTIPLE 1.0, A JUDGEMENT: AZD1163 takes within ACPA-positive RA the share Kevzara took of all RA. CROSS-CHECKS: 2020 gives 11,502 (0.790%) and 2022 gives 14,392 (0.988%). A free fit of the engine's own identity to 2018 to 2021 (2018 and 2019 at the 2020 price, since the CMS file starts in 2020) gives a penetration of 0.00493 with a near-instant ramp (k 3.9, midpoint -0.5), rmse 0.025 points, within 5% of this figure. new_note: Judgement: a multiple of 1.0. Verquvo is the last branded add-on launched into the same patients, labelled for use following a hospitalisation for heart failure or need for outpatient IV diuretics in adults with ejection fraction below 45% (openFDA label, effective 2026-01-21), the post-event setting BalanceD-HF enrols. Corroboration: Kerendia, the same MR prescribing decision, fitted the same way to 25,931, 63,625, 88,208 and 121,794 Part D beneficiaries (2022 to 2025) over its CKD with type 2 diabetes pool of 11.07mm (41% of the book's 27.0mm adults with type 2 diabetes), gives 0.00965 (k 0.74, midpoint 1.335, rmse 3,141); its 2025 point carries half a year of the heart failure label, and on 2022 to 2024 alone the fit gives 0.00567. The value written before, 0.0063, was solved on a logistic fitted to Kerendia's beneficiary stock and then used as the penetration ramp, which reads a stock as penetration. Both numerators are Medicare Part D only, so both understate an all-payer capture. The modelled US treated stock settles near 19,000 by year 7. Case for higher: AstraZeneca's own $3-5bn non-risk-adjusted peak year revenue for balcinrenone/dapagliflozin (Investor Day 2024, BioPharmaceuticals presentation p19) rests on 12 million patients with heart failure and CKD in the top eight markets (p18), a count with no recent-event filter stated, and on the CKD indication as well; it is the company's figure, not an independent forecast, and no broker or aggregator peak was found (GlobalData's likelihood-of-approval page on pharmaceutical-technology.com gives none). AstraZeneca can also move patients from its own dapagliflozin franchise to one capsule, a channel Bayer did not have for Kerendia. Case for lower: finerenone will have been labelled in heart failure for three years by launch, and the MR component faces generic spironolactone and eplerenone

new_note: THE LINE TO ARGUE WITH, and why the plug exists. Penetration is solved to Bank of America's $6bn peak, and the modelled pool cannot reach it at the book's convention price: at $81,962 list the build saturates at $6,375mm of peak revenue even at 99% penetration, because 160,000 metastatic HR-positive HER2-negative patients times 0.7 eligible is 112,000 people. At the convention price and the stated penetration the value halves, rNPV $2,615mm against $5,230mm. The published peak spans SERENA-6 and SERENA-4, and SERENA-4 is first-line disease across a far larger population than this row models, so the honest reading is that the peak is right and the pool is too narrow for it, not that the price is double. The fix is a first-line indication row sized from SEER, after which this price should return to 1.0
new_source: judgement: TWICE Truqap's $81,962 a Medicare beneficiary (CMS Part D 2024, $184,169,026 over 2,247), AstraZeneca's own oral oncology product, so that the NET price at the 0.5 convention equals the CMS figure. This is a plug, and every other CMS-priced seed in the book carries its comparator at 1.0, not 2.0: 39 of the 40 that quote a per-beneficiary figure

new_note: the progression, death and unfitness that keep patients from consolidation are left in the pool and carried by the penetration anchor below, which is measured on the same concurrent chemoradiation starters. SEER's window is 2000 to 2013, before durvalumab; over it the stage IIIA share of the cohort rose from 33.2% to 46.5% (Hansen RN et al.), so the mix is still moving
new_source: Two shares multiplied. (1) Unresectable stage III NSCLC given chemotherapy and radiation as first treatment is 5.369% of all lung cancer diagnoses: of 239,602 lung cancers in SEER over 2000 to 2013, 33,507 were unresectable stage III NSCLC and 12,865 received chemotherapy and radiation (Hansen RN et al., BMC Cancer 2020;20:276, PMC7132866). Over the NSCLC pool that is 5.369% / 0.85 = 6.317%. (2) Concurrent rather than sequential: 35,534 of 42,220 patients given chemoradiation for non-surgically treated stage III NSCLC in the National Cancer Database received it concurrently, 84.2% (Miller ED et al., Radiat Oncol 2018;13:196, PMC6173899: 13,940 of 16,668 elderly and 21,594 of 25,552 younger). PACIFIC-9 enrols patients who have not progressed after concurrent platinum chemoradiation. 0.06317 x 0.8416 = 0.0532, about 10,250 patients a year

new_note: the 0.5 multiple is the most arguable figure here. Durvalumab's own uptake in this setting was immediate: 60.4% of potentially eligible Flatiron patients in the first three months after approval, 66.5% over 18 months (Jairam V et al., J Clin Oncol 2021;39(15_suppl):e20550)
new_source: ANCHOR, measured: 262 of 426 US patients with unresectable stage III NSCLC who started concurrent chemoradiation, 61.5%, went on to consolidation durvalumab (Arunachalam A et al., PLoS One 2024;19(11):e0314156, PMC11588217, US Oncology Network, starts 2017 to 2019); death (28.3%) and progression (22.2%) were the main reasons the rest did not. That is Imfinzi's own capture of this pool, the slot oleclumab would share. MULTIPLE 0.5, A JUDGEMENT: 0.5 x 61.5% = 30.75% of each year's patients at peak. For: AstraZeneca owns the backbone and would move its own consolidation patients; in COAST the combination's PFS hazard ratio against durvalumab alone was 0.44 (Barlesi F et al., Future Oncol 2024, doi:10.1080/14796694.2024.2354160); and a rival add-on trial in this setting, PACIFIC-8 with domvanalimab, was discontinued for strategic portfolio prioritisation (appendix of 27 July 2026). Against: the monalizumab arm of the same trial could take the slot instead; a blinded Phase 3 effect is usually smaller than an open-label Phase 2 one; the combination adds infusions in the first two cycles; and Tagrisso's US label now covers EGFR-mutant unresectable stage III disease after chemoradiation (DailyMed, in the book's labels table), which takes those patients out of durvalumab consolidation after the 2017 to 2019 measurement
new_unit: share of each year's eligible patients

new_note: case for faster: durvalumab reached 60% of eligible patients within three months of its 2018 approval (Jairam V et al.), and an add-on to a backbone the same company sells needs no new prescribers

new_note: the HRRm cohort only: AMPLITUDE, the one PARP add-on Phase 3 in this setting to report, was run in HRR-altered men, and EvoPAR-Prostate01's non-HRRm cohort would take the pool to all 40,200 if it reads out positive. Cross-check on the same basis: 79.3% of first-line mCRPC patients came from mHSPC (Hooper 2026), so 0.115 x 0.793 = 9.11% of diagnoses reach mCRPC from mHSPC, 71% of the 12.81% entering it, which leaves room for deaths before castration resistance. Devasia back-calculates from 2000 to 2017 SEER data and distant-stage incidence rose 5.3% a year in men 45 to 74 and 6.5% in men 75 and over to 2018 (Desai et al., JAMA Netw Open 2022, jamanetwork.com/journals/jamanetworkopen/fullarticle/2790041), so the pool leans low. The case for a smaller pool: AMPLITUDE enrolled every protocol-defined HRR alteration, 56% of them BRCA1 or BRCA2, yet FDA approved Akeega only 'for the treatment of patients with BRCA2-mutated metastatic castration-sensitive prostate cancer' (Johnson & Johnson press release, 2025-12-12), so a saruparib label narrower than the HRRm cohort is a live risk
new_source: Two shares multiplied. First, 12.81% of diagnoses enter metastatic castration-sensitive disease each year. 6.8% of US cases are metastatic at diagnosis and de novo cases are 45% of the men living with metastatic prostate cancer (Devasia et al., Cancer Epidemiol Biomarkers Prev 2023;32(5):659-65, doi:10.1158/1055-9965.EPI-22-1038, PMC10159917; its base case gives de novo and recurrent disease the same survival, so the incidence split is the prevalence split): 0.068 / 0.45 = 15.11% of diagnoses become metastatic. Less the men whose first metastases are already castration-resistant: 1,019 of 5,096 US patients starting first-line mCRPC therapy (20.0%) came from non-metastatic CRPC (Flatiron; Hooper et al., JAMA Netw Open 2026;9(6):e2620750, doi:10.1001/jamanetworkopen.2026.20750), on the book's 11.5% mCRPC share: 0.1511 - 0.115 x 0.200 = 12.81%, about 40,200 men a year. Second, 17.86% carry a protocol-defined HRR alteration: 1,054 of 5,903 men with mCSPC prescreened for AMPLITUDE with a valid result (Attard et al., Nat Med 2025, doi:10.1038/s41591-025-03961-8). 0.1281 x 0.1786 = 0.02288, about 7,180 men a year

new_note: analogue, the most arguable figure here. The ratio does not depend on the Spanish positivity rate: Adelphi's own pooled figures, HRR alterations known in 13% of mCSPC and 18% of mCRPC patients, give (0.13 / 0.1786) x (0.07 / 0.18) = 0.283, and its 38% positivity among the men tested says testing is selective, which a ratio of the two settings absorbs. The case for more: HRR gene testing in metastatic prostate cancer rose 17 points, 26% to 43%, between the 2020 and 2022-2023 waves of the same programme and AMPLITUDE supports testing as routine in mCSPC; saruparib is PARP1-selective, where 25% of AMPLITUDE's niraparib arm needed a transfusion. The case for less: this gives saruparib the whole PARP class, and FDA approved Akeega (niraparib with abiraterone) in BRCA2-mutated mCSPC on 2025-12-12 (Johnson & Johnson press release), so saruparib would launch as the second PARP option in the setting; Akeega reached 93 Medicare Part D beneficiaries in 2025 (CMS file 4ff7c618); and in first-line mCRPC, where the PARP and ARPI combinations are labelled, PARP-based regimens stayed under 2.5% of starts across 2021 to 2025 (Hooper 2026)
new_source: Decomposed into who is found and who is treated once found, on US rates because the model and the treatment share are US. Found: 39% of US men with mCSPC had HRR genes tested in the 2022-2023 wave of the Adelphi Real World Prostate Cancer Disease Specific Programme (Future Oncol 2025, doi:10.1080/14796694.2025.2577337, PMC12622337: HRR gene testing rates 'were highest in the United States (mCSPC: 27% and 39%; mCRPC: 37% and 53%)' in the 2020 and 2022-2023 waves; the 34% and 47% the paper reports overall pool France, Germany and the US). Treated once found: in the 2024 US Flatiron cohort PARP-based regimens were 24 of 344 second-line mCRPC starts, 7.0% (Hooper et al. 2026), against 53% of US mCRPC patients tested for HRR genes (Adelphi, same wave) and 18% of tested mCRPC patients carrying an alteration (1,412 centrally tested mCRPC samples, Cancers 2026;18(10):1614, doi:10.3390/cancers18101614), so PARP starts in that line equal 0.07 / (0.53 x 0.18) = 73.4% of the men known to carry one. 0.39 x 0.734 = 0.286 of each year's HRRm mCSPC men, about 2,050 starts a year at peak. No verifiable independent forecast covers the prostate indication: GlobalData's analyst consensus of $628mm of global sales in 2030 (Clinical Trials Arena, GlobalData Healthcare comment, 2025-06-04, clinicaltrialsarena.com/analyst-comment/asco-2025-akeega-parp-therapy-mcspc/) and a US figure from its expiry model ($340mm in 2036, seen only in a search summary of a page that could not be opened) both span every indication, so neither is solved to

new_note: cross-checked: Sanofi puts the Dupixent COPD label pool at approximately 300,000 US adults at 300 cells/uL and above, which is 21% of the 1,428,571, against a measured 26.6% at that threshold in 34,391 US COPD patients (Mullerova 2019). The chain is consistent within about 25%. It leans low, because GSK's denominator is triple therapy while the trials enrolled inhaled standard care including dual
new_source: GSK states that approximately 70% of US COPD patients inadequately controlled on inhaled triple therapy who continue to exacerbate have a blood eosinophil count of 150 cells/uL and above, and that this group represents over a million people (GSK release 2025-05-22, citing GSK Optum Analysis DOF 2024N562932_00 and Mullerova H et al., Int J Chron Obstruct Pulmon Dis 2019). So the all-eosinophil exacerbating pool is 1,000,000 / 0.70 = 1,428,571, and 1,428,571 / 14,200,000 diagnosed US COPD adults = 0.1006. That is the OBERON and TITANIA entry criterion

new_note: THIS IS THE WEAKEST INPUT IN THE ROW AND IT IS A CONVENTION, NOT A MEASUREMENT. COPD is not a disease whose prevalent pool turns over annually, the way idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis is, and no US COPD incidence sits beside the BRFSS prevalence. The solve behind the penetration assumes a constant eligible pool each year, which is what this produces. State a real incidence and the penetration has to be re-solved
new_source: stated equal to prevalence, which sets the engine's carryover to zero, so the penetration is the share of each year's eligible patients started rather than a share of an accumulating pool

new_note: the 1.0 multiple is a judgement, argued from OBERON and TITANIA cutting exacerbations 29% and 34% across all eosinophil counts against Dupixent at 300 cells/uL and above and Nucala at 150 and above. TWO DISCLOSURES, BOTH POINTING DOWN. Dupixent is absent from the class denominator at 88,374 Part D beneficiaries that cannot be split across its six indications, and it is the actual COPD competitor, so including any of it cuts Tezspire's share. And Park's 11.9% is a 2018 to 2021 baseline being applied to a 2028 launch
new_source: Tezspire's measured class capture, at a 1.0 multiple. Tezspire held 16.94% of the US biologic asthma class in 2024 (13,837 Medicare beneficiaries of 81,661 across Tezspire, Nucala, Fasenra and Xolair), and 11.9% of severe asthma patients are on any biologic (Park et al., J Asthma Allergy 2026;19, doi 10.2147/JAA.S580937, 2,827 patients, 5.2% at GINA step 4 and 19.6% at step 5). 0.119 x 0.1694 = 2.02% of the pool, solved back through the curve and a 25.4% discontinuation to a peak of 0.02039

new_note: chosen over one_time, as mrk_zilovertamab_vedotin.csv and abbv_abbv_rgx_314.csv do for a course, so cost of sales rides as Biogen's filed share of revenue and is eroded with revenue after LOE; one_time needs a per-patient cost of goods, which Biogen does not disclose
new_source: a single course: PREVAIL gives felzartamab or placebo as intravenous infusions over a 24-week treatment period, then follows patients to week 104 (ClinicalTrials.gov NCT06935357, checked 2026-09-26). Run as chronic with every patient stopping inside the year (discontinuation_pct 1.0 below), which the engine builds exactly as one_time, the year's new patients times the price of a course

new_note: THE MOST ARGUABLE FIGURE HERE. Felzartamab has no price. Biogen may price a durable plasma-cell course against the chronic B-cell class rather than against a steroid: Voyxact lists at $390,000 a year (ICER Table E2.3, $30,000 every four weeks), so a course priced at one year of Voyxact would be 2.36x this. IGNAZ's nine-dose arm cut UPCR 29.5% against 5.7% on placebo at nine months and was still 44.5% down at 24 months, 18 months off drug (Phase 2a, PubMed 40581166), which is the case for a price above Tarpeyo's
new_source: Tarpeyo (Nefecon, delayed-release budesonide), the only IgA nephropathy therapy sold as a single finite course: WAC $17,850 per one-month package (RedBook) and 9.25 packages to a course, $165,113 (ICER, B-Cell Directed Therapies for IgA Nephropathy, Final Report, 31 March 2026, Table E2.3; icer.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/ICER_IgAN_Final-Report_For_Publication_033126.pdf). The match is on disease and on the shape of treatment: NefIgArd gave nine months of drug then 15 months off it, PREVAIL gives 24 weeks then 80 weeks off it. Cross-check: CMS Medicare Quarterly Part D Spending by Drug (4ff7c618-4e40-483a-b390-c8a58c94fa15), Tarpeyo 2025 Q1-Q4, $65,037,010.56 over 3,758 claims is $17,306.28 a claim, 3.0% below the package WAC; 2026 Q1 is $18,153.81. Spend per beneficiary ($95,642.66 over 680) is a part-course figure, since a nine-month course straddles calendar years, so it is not used

new_note: the comparator's own forecast discount on the list this row prices from. Felzartamab is an infusion, bought on the medical benefit where the Part B basis is ASP; a smaller discount than a Part D oral carries would lift the net. The book's 0.5 is calibrated on CMS per-beneficiary gross and does not apply to a WAC
new_source: ICER Final Report, 31 March 2026, Table E2.3: IPD Analytics forecasts a 19% discount from WAC for Nefecon in 2025, a net course price of $133,741, the figure ICER's budget impact uses

new_source: ANCHOR: the book's Filspari capture, 0.0162, the peak the engine needs to reproduce Filspari's measured take (povetacicept and zigakibart seeds, which solved it through the engine). I checked its inputs: Filspari US net product sales of $322mm in FY2025 (Travere 8-K 0001438533-26-000013, exhibit 99.1). Because this is a course, what counts is starts. The engine's stock path at 0.0162, 219, 828 and 2,047 (zigakibart seed), implies starts of about 219, 669 and 1,447 at 27.5% stopping, against Filspari's measured 186, 706 and 1,438, so the peak is a starts rate and transfers to a course without restating. MULTIPLE 0.4186, DERIVED: felzartamab is the fifth B-cell-directed entrant, after Voyxact (approved 25 November 2025), Trutakna (July 2026), povetacicept (PDUFA 30 November 2026) and zigakibart (BEYOND reads out H1 2027, before PREVAIL completes). Under the order-of-entry penalty of Urban et al., Management Science 1986 (share of about entry order^-0.49), a fifth entrant holds 0.4545 / (1 + 0.7120 + 0.5837 + 0.5070 + 0.4545 = 3.2572) = 13.95% of the class. new_note: JUDGEMENT on the line. QUINTESSENTIAL's primary endpoint is in patients after four or more prior lines, the population FDA wrote the first labels of Abecma, Carvykti, Tecvayli, Talvey and Elrexfio to, so the fifth-line share is taken. BMS names the setting 4L+ and the trial met response after three or more lines as a secondary; the fourth-line share is (2,971 + 954) / 24,825 = 15.81%, and the uptake anchor below is struck on the same fifth-line pool, so choosing the wider pool would lower the capture and leave modelled patients about the same. Not taken off: prior BCMA-targeted therapy, which the label will likely require (no US share of fifth-line patients with BCMA exposure was found), and prior GPRC5D therapy, which the trial excludes. Fonseca counts treated patients in data to 2018; longer survival on newer regimens may take more patients to a fifth line
new_source: Fonseca R et al., 'Frontline treatment patterns and attrition rates by subsequent lines of therapy in patients with newly diagnosed multiple myeloma', BMC Cancer 2020;20:1087, doi:10.1186/s12885-020-07503-y (PMC7656738), Table 4, three US databases 2000 to 2018: of 22,062 patients treated without a transplant 1,706 reached a fifth line, and of 2,763 with a transplant 618 did. (1,706 + 618) / (22,062 + 2,763) = 2,324 / 24,825 = 9.36%, about 3,370 of the 36,000 a year

new_note: The judgement is taking one product's measured share, not the class's 53.61%. Case for higher: arlo-cel would be the only CAR T for patients already given a BCMA-targeted therapy, and BMS has added cell therapy capacity since 2023. Case for lower: both 2023 products were supply-constrained, so the anchor measures slots as much as demand; Talvey (GPRC5D bispecific, 692 Part B beneficiaries in 2024) already treats this setting and its patients are excluded; BCMA bispecifics and newer CAR Ts compete for the same patients. Modelled peak about 903 US infusions a year, $464mm US at the 2025 net price and about $632mm with ex-US, before BMS's costs
new_source: ANCHOR, the per-product capture of the two myeloma CAR Ts in 2023, the last full year both were labelled only after four or more prior lines: Abecma was approved in March 2021 after four or more prior lines (BMS FY2021 10-K 0000014272-22-000051) and widened to two or more in April 2024 (BMS FY2024 10-K 0000014272-25-000039), and the Johnson & Johnson FY2023 10-K (0000200406-24-000013) lists Carvykti's one to three prior lines indication (CARTITUDE-4) as filed, not approved. US net sales: Abecma $358mm (BMS FY2023 10-K 0000014272-24-000044, alliance note), Carvykti $469mm (Johnson & Johnson, book asset_revenue_regions, SEC financial statement data sets). Net per infusion in 2023: Carvykti's CMS Part B $29,109,653 over 60 beneficiaries (drug_demand) = $485,160.88, divided by 1.06 = $457,698.95; Abecma has no 2023 Part B row and is taken at the same price (its 2024 row, $486,972, is within 0.4% of Carvykti's). Patients: Abecma 358 / 0.457699 = 782; Carvykti 469 / 0.457699 = 1,025. Over the fifth-line pool of 3,370 (36,000 x 0.093615): 23.21% and 30.40%, a mean of 26.81% a product. MULTIPLE 1.0, A JUDGEMENT

Case for less: amivantamab is already given in this line (3 of 40 second lines in the Rafizadeh cohort, where chemotherapy took 30), sacituzumab tirumotecan's TroFuse-009 tests the same comparison and completes in August 2028 (the sacituzumab tirumotecan seed), and first-line osimertinib combinations change who reaches this line

new_note: the 0.4 multiple is the arguable figure. new_note: stated on the filing, since the asset is outside the gate model (not big pharma) and the published NDA/BLA-to-approval rate assumes no negative vote. The case for lower: this is the second review after a complete response letter on effectiveness (July 2025), the hierarchy broke at LVEF (p=0.09) so the other secondary endpoints are nominal, the study is one trial of 106, and a BIMO inspection left a Form 483 on trial conduct. The study read the 18 human drug advisory committees; the Cellular, Tissue and Gene Therapies committee that voted here is a CBER committee and not one of them

new_source: BALANCE (clinicaltrials.gov/api/v2/studies/NCT07519395, read 2026-09-26): a 26-week, two-part, dose-ranging trial of three dose levels of camlipixant against placebo in adults with IBS-D or IBS-M, primary endpoint change in weekly abdominal pain intensity over weeks 7 to 12. The cough trials gave it at 25 mg and 50 mg twice daily (6-K 0001654954-26-006705)

new_note: Judgement on the comparator. Viberzi is the only branded oral drug labelled for IBS-D that is taken continuously for abdominal pain and diarrhoea (openFDA label: 100 mg twice daily, adults with IBS-D); IBS-M has no approved drug, so one price covers both pools. Xifaxan ran $11,552.39 a 2025 beneficiary (118,572 beneficiaries, same dataset), but its label also covers travellers' diarrhoea and hepatic encephalopathy, so its per-beneficiary figure is not an IBS price. A beneficiary filled about 5.2 claims in 2025 (33,838 over 6,480), so this is part-year spend, which is the convention's point
new_source: Viberzi (eluxadoline), CMS Part D quarterly dataset 4ff7c618-4e40-483a-b390-c8a58c94fa15, row '2025 (Q1-Q4)': $59,881,667.51 over 6,480 beneficiaries = $9,241.00 a beneficiary, taken as it stands and not annualised. In GBP because the engine models a company in its reporting currency: $9,241.00 at GBP/USD 1.325237 (ECB via fetchers/fx_ecb.py, fx_rates row of 2026-09-25) is GBP 6,973.09

new_note: convention; the capture anchor below is struck at this same net of $4,620.50 a patient-year, so the two move together
new_source: Part D gross-to-net convention, measured at a median 96% of CMS's own negotiated net annual prices across the nine cycle-one IRA drugs (backend/gross_to_net.py)

new_note: Arithmetic on CMS counts under a steady-state assumption. Viberzi's beneficiaries fell from 8,693 in 2020 to 6,935 in 2024 (drug_demand), and a shrinking stock means this slightly understates stopping. It is the rate the capture anchor below is computed at, so the two are a pair
new_source: Measured on the comparator, drug_demand Viberzi Part D 2024: 2,262,474 tablets over 6,935 beneficiaries at two tablets a day (the label dose) is 163.1 days on drug a beneficiary, 44.69% of a year. With a steady stock, a year's beneficiaries are the patients on drug at its start plus that year's starts, and only those still on drug at its end carry into the next, so the share not carried is 1 - 0.4469 = 0.5531. Claims agree: 34,827 claims of 65.0 tablets each is 5.0 thirty-day fills a beneficiary

new_note: Could slip a year if GSK waits for BALANCE's full completion (2027-07-13) or runs a longer Phase 3 than eluxadoline's
new_source: Judgement from two dated analogues, since no Phase 3 is registered and GSK gives no timing. (1) Camlipixant's own last step: Phase 2b SOOTHE (NCT04678206) reached primary completion on 2021-10-21 and Phase 3 CALM-1 (NCT05599191) started on 2022-10-25, twelve months later, so BALANCE's 2027-03-09 primary completion puts a Phase 3 start in 2028. (2) Eluxadoline, the comparator: its first Phase 3 (NCT01553591) started on 2012-05-29 and 2016 was its first full year on sale (Allergan 10-K 0001564590-17-002433: US revenue $12.3mm in 2015, $93.3mm in 2016), four years. 2028 + 4 = 2032

new_note: The multiple is the most arguable figure here. For 1.0: camlipixant would enter the same position Viberzi did, a new mechanism for IBS pain, and it does not share the mu-opioid mechanism behind Viberzi's pancreatitis and severe constipation warnings, nor its contraindication in patients without a gallbladder (openFDA label, sections 4 and 5). The case for lower: the rate is applied to IBS-M, where no drug has shown what capture looks like; P2X3 antagonism showed limited efficacy in cough (6-K 0001654954-26-006705); GSK valued the IBS programme at only GBP 104mm after the cough result. The case for higher: Viberzi's revenue grew partly on price, so its patient capture is if anything understated here. On this row the US line plateaus near 92,600 patients, 2.3 times Viberzi's 2019 stock, because the pool includes IBS-M
new_source: ANCHOR, the capture_anchor identity applied to Viberzi, the last branded chronic IBS-D launch, at this row's own net price. US revenue (Allergan 10-Ks 0001564590-17-002433, 0001564590-18-002345, 0001564590-19-003111, 0001564590-20-005038): 2016 $93.3mm, 2017 $156.6mm, 2018 $176.5mm, 2019 $187.9mm. Net a patient-year $4,620.50 (0.5 x $9,241.00), so stocks of 20,193, 33,892, 38,199 and 40,667. Stopping 55.31% a year (the row above): starts 2016 20,193; 2017 33,892 - 20,193 x 0.4469 = 24,868; 2018 23,053; 2019 23,595. Pool: the IBS-D share of the Rome IV pool, 16,285,674 x 0.281 = 4,576,274, shrunk by cumulative starts. Capture 0.441%, 0.546%, 0.509% and 0.523%; 2019, the latest year, is taken, as capture_anchor takes its latest. MULTIPLE 1.0, A JUDGEMENT

new_note: A midpoint before the first full year means the capture rate is near its plateau from year one, which is what Viberzi's own capture did (0.441% in its first full year against 0.523% in its fourth). Amgen's US Tezspire sales were $1,478mm in 2025 (10-K 0000318154-26-000010) and $486mm in Q2 2026 (10-Q 0000318154-26-000126, inline XBRL, country US), x4 = $1,944mm. At 25.37% stopping, 2026 new starts = 114,945 - 87,391 x 0.7463 = 49,725, which is 7.72% of the 644,112 biologic-eligible severe asthma pool the book carries on tilrekimig and felcorekibart (23,004,000 US adults with current asthma, CDC NHIS 2023, x 2.8% eligible for at least one biologic, Akenroye et al., J Allergy Clin Immunol 2020;145(4):1295-1297, doi:10.1016/j.jaci.2019.12.009). At carryover 0 the penetration is the share of each year's eligible patients. MULTIPLE 0.20, A JUDGEMENT, as on lunsekimig and AZD6793: 0.20 x 7.72% = 1.544%. Case for more: dosing every three months against tozorakimab's four weeks, a mechanism GSK argues reaches the non-type-2 majority of COPD, and GSK's COPD sales force behind Trelegy and Nucala. Case against: no efficacy is disclosed in COPD, where the only data are a Phase 1 repeat-dose part; it is the second anti-IL-33 ligand antibody, about four years behind tozorakimab; the class has failed before, since Sanofi and Regeneron stopped itepekimab in COPD after AERIFY-1 and -2 (the book's retired programmes, asset 2791); and it launches around 2032 behind Dupixent, Nucala, Exdensur, tozorakimab, felcorekibart and lunsekimig.

Elahere (mirvetuximab soravtansine, the marketed FRalpha ADC in platinum-resistant ovarian cancer, HCPCS J9063). CMS Medicare Part B quarterly file, 2025 (Q1-Q4), dataset bf6a5b3b-31ee-4abb-b1ad-2607a1e7510a: $232,480,864.62 over 1,884 beneficiaries = $123,397.49 a beneficiary. Converted at ECB GBP/USD 1.327632344386271 (fetchers/fx_ecb.py, 2026-09-23). The 2024 annual Part B figure was $121,204 (1,757 beneficiaries); 2025 is used because it exists. This is a per-beneficiary figure, not per claim: Elahere is in its third full year, not a launch year. The engine reads one price per asset, so this also prices the endometrial row. The endometrial alternative is Enhertu 2025 Part B: $72,455.15 a beneficiary = GBP 54,574.71.

Social Security Act section 1847A: Medicare Part B pays 106% of average sales price, and ASP is already net of manufacturer discounts and rebates, so the manufacturer's price is the CMS figure divided by 1.06, which is 5.66% below it

new_source: MIRASOL (Moore et al., N Engl J Med 2023, PMID 38055253): median PFS of 5.62 months on mirvetuximab in FRalpha-high PROC. At a constant hazard, 0.5^(12/5.62) = 22.76% remain on therapy after a year, so 77.24% stop. No median PFS is published for mocertatug, and duration of response has not been reached. Discontinuation is one asset-level value, so it also serves the endometrial row.

new_source: SEER 2026 new ovarian cancers, equal to the raludotatug deruxtecan rows
SEER 2026

SEER Cancer Stat Facts, ovary, 2026: 12,450 deaths over 21,010 new cases. The argument: platinum-resistant disease is incurable and nearly every ovarian cancer death passes through it, so in a steady state the patients entering PROC each year roughly equal the deaths. This is an UPPER BOUND. It includes deaths never treated in the line, and both trials exclude primary platinum-refractory disease and require ECOG 0-1. The published alternative, Kumar et al. (ISPOR 2024, doi:10.1016/j.jval.2024.03.1253, poster), counts 917 + 1,895 + 1,715 = 4,527 PROC regimens in lines 2 to 4+ on 23,820 incident cases, a share of 0.1901. The revenue data rule it out: Elahere's 4,142 US starts in 2025 would be 104% of that all-comers count, although Elahere's label covers only the 36% who are FRalpha-high.

new_note: the 0.4 multiple is a judgement
new_source: This reproduces the identity in backend/capture_anchor.py on Elahere. US revenue comes from AbbVie filings: - FY2025: $607mm (10-K 0001551152-26-000008). - FY2024: $477mm, counted only from the 12 Feb 2024 ImmunoGen close (324 of 366 days), annualised to $538.8mm. - 2026: Q2 US $161mm (10-Q 0001551152-26-000026) x 4 = $644mm. Net price per patient-year = the Part B figure / 1.06: $114,344 for 2024 and $116,413 for 2025. Stock = revenue / net price: 4,712 (2024), 5,214 (2025), 5,532 (2026, at the 2025 price). Starts = this year's stock less last year's stock x (1 - 0.7724): - 2025: 5,214 - 1,073 = 4,142. - 2026: 5,532 - 1,187 = 4,345. The all-comers PROC cohort is 21,010 x 0.5926 = 12,450. Elahere's starts are 0.3327 of it in 2025 and 0.3490 in 2026. On Elahere's own label (FRalpha-high, 36% of PROC: Matulonis et al., JCO 2023, doi:10.1200/JCO.22.01900; 36.3% in the real world: Previs et al., Gynecol Oncol 2024, doi:10.1016/j.ygyno.2024.11.010), the same starts are 92.4% and 97.0% of 4,482 a year. The incumbent has filled its niche. Peak = anchor 0.3327 (2025, the last full reported year) x multiple 0.4. The multiple is a JUDGEMENT. Case for a higher multiple: the label covers all comers with no B7-H4 cut-off. Confirmed ORR was 62% (21/34 at 5.8 mg/kg) against Elahere's 42% in MIRASOL. B7-H4 is a new target, so it can follow an FRalpha ADC. Case against: the PROC launch is about 2032, behind four rivals: - Genmab's Rina-S, an FRalpha ADC (NCT06619236, primary completion 2027-02). - R-DXd from Daiichi Sankyo and Merck (REJOICE-Ovarian01, NCT06161025, 2028-02, Breakthrough). - AZD5335 (NCT07218809, 2028-11). - Sofetabart (2030). The 62% comes from 34 patients at one dose in a single-arm trial. Elahere is modelled off its own revenue, so any share taken from it is counted twice. Carryover: at 0 (the engine's documented setting for a line of cancer therapy), the penetration is a share of each year's cohort. At the book default of 1.0, this drug's own curve converges on the whole cohort: an engine run gives about $1.8bn US at year 10, against $245mm at carryover 0. Elahere sells $607mm in the US.

new_note: 2.4 fitted plus two years, because the ovarian launch follows the asset's 2030 start by two
new_source: Enhertu, an infused DXd ADC with a topoisomerase payload billed under Part B. CMS Part B beneficiaries: 864, 1,904, 4,841, 7,105 and 8,410 (2020-2024 annual file), then 10,461 (2025 quarterly file). A logistic fitted over 2020-2025 gives k 0.97, midpoint 2.4 years, plateau 10,900, rmse 365 beneficiaries (3.5% of the 2025 level). The book's k 1.08 / midpoint 2.2 on the same six points gives rmse 396. Elahere's own series cannot be fitted: J9063 took effect on 1 July 2023, so its 2023 count of 972 covers half a year, leaving two clean points (1,757 and 1,884, up only 7%). That flat second year suggests PROC ADC uptake saturates quickly.

In GBP because GSK reports in sterling: USD 109,433.62 / 1.327632344386271 (GBP/USD, ECB via fetchers/fx_ecb.py, 2026-09-23) = GBP 82,427.65, so 0.082428 mm GBP per year. Imdelltra is the marketed second-line ES-SCLC incumbent: same disease, same line, infused under Part B. It is not an ADC. drug_demand holds no Part B row for it, which is why ABBV-706 used Trodelvy; the 2025 companion file now has one. 2025 is its first full year, not its launch year (launched May 2024). At 7.06 claims a beneficiary against a 4.2-month median PFS, the figure is close to a whole course, so the per-beneficiary default stands. Alternatives, same file, 2025: Trodelvy (topoisomerase-1 ADC, the class) $86,033.17 = GBP 64,801.95; Enhertu $72,455.15 = GBP 54,574.71; Zepzelca (lurbinectedin, second-line SCLC) $58,336.21 = GBP 43,940.04.

Social Security Act section 1847A: Medicare Part B pays 106% of average sales price, and ASP is already net of manufacturer discounts and rebates, so the manufacturer's price is the CMS figure divided by 1.06, which is 5.66% below it

The ABBV-706 funnel, with its third-line step swapped for the second-line one. SCLC was 11.8% of new US lung cancers in 2019, and 70.9% of SCLC was extensive-stage at diagnosis (Wells et al., JTO Clin Res Rep 2025, doi:10.1016/j.jtocrr.2025.100799, SEER 17; checked against the full text). Of 2,573 US patients with extensive-stage SCLC given first-line platinum, 992 (38.6%) received at least one further line (Sankar et al., Adv Ther 2025, doi:10.1007/s12325-025-03408-z, Flatiron 2018-2023; checked against the full text). 0.118 x 0.709 x 0.386 = 0.0323, about 7,319 patients a year. EMBOLD-SCLC-301 enrols after one platinum + PD-(L)1 line and admits prior tarlatamab, so second and third line. It excludes limited-stage disease at diagnosis, prior topoisomerase-1 ADCs and B7-H3 agents; those exclusions are not taken off. The eligible share of 0.0323 contains ABBV-706's 0.01121, the third-line patients, in full.

new_note: the 0.25 multiple is a judgement for a third novel second-line agent
new_source: ANCHOR, the capture_anchor identity applied to Imdelltra. US revenue $115mm in 2024 and $513mm in 2025 (Amgen 10-K 0000318154-26-000010); $233mm in Q2 2026 and $421mm in H1 (10-Q 0000318154-26-000126). Net per patient = $109,433.62 x (1 - 0.056604) = $103,239. Stock: 1,114; 4,969; 9,028 on the 2026 quarter x 4. Stopping 86.20% a year: DeLLphi-304 median PFS 4.2 months (Mountzios et al., N Engl J Med 2025, doi:10.1056/NEJMoa2502099, as reported at ASCO 2025 LBA8008), so 0.5^(12/4.2) = 13.80% remain. New starts: 2025 = 4,969 - 1,114 x 0.1380 = 4,815; 2026 = 9,028 - 4,969 x 0.1380 = 8,342 (7,470 on the half year x 2). The pool is the annual second-line ES-SCLC cohort, 7,319, with carryover 0 as the engine applies it here. Capture: 15.2% in the 2024 part year, 65.8% in 2025, and 114.0% in 2026 (102.1% on the half year). Above 100% is a finding, not a share. Imdelltra alone already starts more patients than the book's funnel says reach second line. The funnel omits relapsed limited-stage disease and the backlog of patients who progressed before its approval, and Sankar's follow-up is truncated. So the anchor is taken from 2025, 65.8%. MULTIPLE 0.25, A JUDGEMENT: 0.25 x 65.8% = 16.4%. The case for: overall survival HR 0.46 against topotecan, median OS 18.5 against 10.3 months, ORR 58.3% against 12.6%, and fewer grade 3+ events (60.9% against 78.2%). The case against: this is the third novel second-line agent. Ifinatamab deruxtecan, a B7-H3 ADC from Merck and Daiichi, has a PDUFA date of 10 October 2026 (Merck 10-Q 0000310158-26-000212), about 2.5 years ahead. Tambotatug pelitecan (YL201, TAISHAN-302) posted the same HR 0.46 on the same day. Imdelltra is entrenched and moving into first line. The only Phase 3 evidence is Chinese, and the global trial admits patients already given tarlatamab, where ADC activity is unmeasured.

new_note: Judgement: this is a published list price, which the book puts ahead of the CMS convention, but it belongs to the comparator and not to velzatinib. Qinlock is the closest marketed KIT inhibitor in GIST. Cross-check on the CMS basis: Qinlock's Medicare Part D 2025 (Q1-Q4) spend was $126,600,395.66 over 536 beneficiaries, $236,194.77 each at 5.25 fills a beneficiary (CMS Part D quarterly dataset 4ff7c618-4e40-483a-b390-c8a58c94fa15). A treated patient in Medicare filled 44% of a year, so this full-year WAC bills each treated patient more than the average Qinlock patient pays in a calendar year; that is the main case for a lower price. Ayvakit, the other branded GIST KIT inhibitor, ran $323,698.51 a 2025 beneficiary, but most of its use is systemic mastocytosis. The generic comparators (sunitinib, imatinib) cost a small fraction of this. A second-line drug may also launch below a fourth-line one. In GBP because the engine models a company in its reporting currency and converts to dollars only at the end: $567,210.00 at GBP/USD 1.327632 (ECB via fetchers/fx_ecb.py, 2026-09-23, the fx_rates row the other GSK seeds use) is GBP 427,234.24
new_source: Deciphera, Information for Colorado Prescribers of Prescription Drugs, v.3 effective 2026-01-01 (https://www.deciphera.com/sites/default/files/2026-01/CO%20Disclosure%20Form%20Final%20v.3%202026.01.01.Q.pdf): Qinlock 50 mg, 90-count bottle, WAC $46,620. Label dose is 150 mg (three tablets) once daily (Qinlock USPI), so one bottle is 30 days: 46,620 x 365/30 = $567,210 a year

new_note: Replaces the 0.2777 reused from Kalydeco, which is a CMS per-beneficiary spend over a WAC and so measures part-year use rather than a discount. The reserves include Deciphera's ex-US rebates, 24% of its 2023 product revenue. This is a floor on the discount for a 2030 launch: the Medicare Part D manufacturer discount program (10% in the initial phase, 20% in the catastrophic phase, which a drug at this price reaches in its first fill) began in 2025, after this measurement, as the osivelotor seed also notes. Net is $457,965 a patient-year
new_source: Measured on the comparator itself: Deciphera's FY2023 10-K (0001654151-24-000004), the last full year it filed before Ono acquired it, reports Qinlock revenue reserves (trade discounts, chargebacks and administrative fees, government rebates, returns) of $37,906k provided on current-year sales plus $49k for prior periods against product revenues, net of $159,074k, all of it Qinlock. Gross sales were 159,074 + 37,955 = $197,029k, so 37,955 / 197,029 = 19.26% came off list. FY2022 on the same basis (0001654151-23-000003): 26,494 / 151,998 = 17.4%

new_note: Constant hazard from a median: 1 - 0.5^(12/13.7) = 0.455, the form the atirmociclib seed uses. The case against: this is a single-arm Phase 1b cohort with a wide CI, first-line PFS was still immature at 7.4 months' follow-up, and sunitinib, the Phase 3 comparator, had a median PFS of 9.2 months in the PEAK control arm (Cogent 8-K, 10 November 2025), which gives 0.595. If velzatinib wins StrateGIST 3, its PFS should sit between the two
new_source: StrateGIST 1 Phase 1b, second-line cohort, ASCO 2026: median PFS 13.7 months (95% CI 8.6-18.4) at 18.4 months' follow-up (OncLive, 'Velzatinib Shows Activity Across Treatment Lines and KIT Mutation Profiles in Advanced GIST'; Targeted Oncology, same meeting)

new_note: The rate is age-adjusted to the 2000 standard and averaged over 2001-2015. It rose about 5% a year over that period (APC 4.44 in males, 5.40 in females), so the current rate is likely higher. The same paper counts 34,257 cases over 15 years, 2,284 a year
new_source: Patel N, Benipal B. Incidence of GIST in the United States 2001-2015: a USCS analysis of 50 states. Cureus 2019;11(2):e4120, doi:10.7759/cureus.4120 (PMID 31037234): overall incidence 0.70 per 100,000 a year, applied to the 340,110,988 US residents of July 2024 (Census Vintage 2024)

new_note: Judgement: assumes every KIT-mutant patient reaching advanced disease eventually fails imatinib and is fit for a second line, and that the label follows the trial's exclusions. The case for lower: adjuvant imatinib now delays or prevents some recurrences, some patients stay on first-line imatinib for years, and some die or decline before second line. The case for higher: the incidence rate is out of date and rising, and non-exon-18 PDGFRA mutants (a share of the 2.1%) are eligible but left out here
new_source: Three sourced parts. (1) 5,234 of 31,019 staged cases (16.87%) were distant at diagnosis (Patel & Benipal, Cureus 2019;11(2):e4120, PMID 31037234, Table 1). (2) Estimated 15-year recurrence-free survival after surgery without adjuvant therapy was 59.9%, so 40.1% recur (Joensuu H et al., Lancet Oncol 2012;13:265-74, doi:10.1016/S1470-2045(11)70299-6, PMID 22153892, 2,560 patients pooled). 0.1687 + 0.8313 x 0.401 = 0.5021 of each year's diagnoses reach advanced disease. (3) The label reach: StrateGIST 3 (NCT07218926; ASCO 2026 TPS11588) excludes GIST that is wild-type for both KIT and PDGFRA and GIST with an activating PDGFRA exon 18 mutation. In advanced GIST (MetaGIST) KIT mutations are found in 82.8% and PDGFRA in 2.1% (Emile JF et al., Med Oncol 2012;29(3):1765-72, doi:10.1007/s12032-011-0074-y, PMID 21953054). 0.5021 x 0.828 = 0.4157

new_note: JUDGEMENT on the multiple, the formula the zigakibart seed cross-checks with. The case for higher: velzatinib is a single agent where the pioneer is a two-drug combination carrying sunitinib's toxicity, its second-line cohort showed a 13.7-month median PFS, and a PFS win could also displace imatinib dose escalation, which the 52.8% leaves out. The case for lower: StrateGIST 3 compares against sunitinib alone, not the combination that will be standard by readout, so velzatinib may launch without a head-to-head answer to it; Hsu's denominator excludes patients who received neither option, so the share overstates capture of this pool; the setting is Taiwan, not the US. Bezuclastinib is not in the book, so pool_crowding cannot see it and the cut has to sit here.
new_source: Two parts. (1) Sunitinib's measured second-line share: Hsu JT et al., Oncotarget 2017;8(41):71128-37, doi:10.18632/oncotarget.16795, PMID 29050348 (Taiwan National Health Insurance Research Database, July 2004 to December 2010): of 521 advanced GIST patients failing first-line imatinib 400 mg and treated with dose escalation or sunitinib, 125 escalated then switched to sunitinib and 150 switched directly, so 275 (52.78%) received sunitinib after imatinib. (2) An order-of-entry cut, because velzatinib will not be the first branded drug to beat sunitinib in second line: Cogent's bezuclastinib plus sunitinib beat sunitinib in the PEAK Phase 3 (median PFS 16.5 against 9.2 months, HR 0.50, Cogent 8-K 10 November 2025) and its NDA was accepted with priority review and a PDUFA date of 2026-11-30 (Cogent release, 28 May 2026), more than three years before velzatinib's 2030 start. Urban et al., Management Science 1986, put a second entrant's share at 2^-0.49 = 0.712 of the pioneer's, so the second of two takes 0.712 / 1.712 = 41.59% of the class. 0.5278 x 0.4159 = 0.2195

new_source: CMS Medicare Part D Quarterly 2025 (Q1 to Q4), dataset 4ff7c618-4e40-483a-b390-c8a58c94fa15, Rexulti (brexpiprazole): $1,127,195,022.03 over 121,062 beneficiaries = $9,310.89 per beneficiary (828,931 claims, $1,359.82 a claim). Not annualised. Rexulti is chosen because its label is the same one seltorexant seeks: an add-on to an antidepressant after inadequate response. Seltorexant's head-to-head comparator, quetiapine XR, is from the same augmentation class. Against the choice: Rexulti's Medicare beneficiaries include schizophrenia and Alzheimer's agitation patients. new_source: Anchor: Elahere's 2025 US starts of 4,142 = 0.3327 of the all-comers PROC cohort of 12,450. The derivation is on GSK's ovarian row: - US revenue: $607mm (2025), $538.8mm (2024, annualised). - Net price: $116,413 per patient-year. - Stock: 5,214 (2025) against 4,712 (2024), with 77.24% stopping. - In 2026 the rate is 0.3490 (Q2 x 4). Peak = 0.3327 x multiple 0.5 = 0.1663. The multiple is a JUDGEMENT. Case for a higher multiple: - Breakthrough designation (20 Jan 2026) after bevacizumab and mirvetuximab. - Activity at every FRalpha level: ORR 40% at 0-24% expression and 54% at 75% or more. - ORR 50% in 104 patients. - An all-comers label about 2.8 times Elahere's FRalpha-high label, and a head-to-head arm against chemotherapy or mirvetuximab. Case against: - Arrives about 2030 into a crowded class. - Genmab's Rina-S is also an FRalpha ADC for all comers and reads out about two years earlier (NCT06619236, 2027-02). - R-DXd PROC (2028-02, Breakthrough) and AZD5335 (2028-11) come first too. - FRAmework-01 excludes patients who had a prior topoisomerase-payload ADC. - Elahere is modelled off its own revenue, so share taken from it is counted twice. The multiple is set above GSK's 0.4 because Sofe-M reaches PROC about two years earlier and holds Breakthrough. Carryover: at 0, this drug's US revenue at year 10 is about $311mm; at the book default of 1.0 it is about $1.8bn, because the curve then converges on the whole cohort.

new_source: ANCHOR, a measured analogue: the PCSK9 inhibitors, the last high-priced injectable lipid class to launch into a prevalent US pool against payer prior authorisation. In one large US cardiology practice, Cardiology Consultants of Philadelphia with 97 cardiologists (Smith A et al., J Clin Med 2021;10:3828, doi:10.3390/jcm10173828, PMC8432238, Table 2) the yearly share of eligible ASCVD patients newly prescribed one was 0.26% in 2015 (from the July launch), 1.23% in 2016, 1.09% in 2017, 1.52% in 2018 and 1.60% in 2019: 45, 216, 196, 286 and 316 patients over 17,267 to 19,689 eligible. That is the engine's penetration itself, new starts over eligible patients, so it is fitted directly: a logistic with peak 0.0142, k 3.06 and midpoint -0.55 years from the first full year (2016) fits the five years to an rmse of 0.17 points, 2015 taken at year -1 as measured and not annualised. MULTIPLE 0.25, A JUDGEMENT: 0.25 x 0.0142 = 0.00355. The case: that rate was a whole class with two drugs; solbinsiran would be the third RNA drug into sHTG after olezarsen (approved June 2026) and plozasiran, both APOC3, which cut triglycerides by about 80% in sHTG (SHASTA-3 and SHASTA-4 medians of 79% and 81%, Arrowhead 10-Q for the quarter to 2026-06-30) against solbinsiran's 58% to 60% in mixed dyslipidaemia (NCT05256654), and olezarsen and plozasiran report fewer pancreatitis events where solbinsiran has no such data. For it: ANGPTL3 silencing also lowered apoB in PROLONG-ANG3 (24.3% at 400 mg against 11.6% on placebo at day 180), a second lipid benefit

new_source: derived: Merck generated $39,599mm of free cash flow on $189,294mm of revenue over 2023, 2024 and 2025, a 20.92% margin, against the 29.5% its cost of sales, SG&A and R&D leave. Solved so the modelled book reproduces that margin rather than assumed from one line's cost structure: the alliance rows carry no cost of sales and Animal Health carries its own, so a ratio taken off a single product does not reconcile the company. The window barely matters here, unlike Pfizer: the same aggregate is 21.9% over five years and 21.3% over every year on file. Restated before interest: MRK paid $3,700mm of interest inside operating cash flow over 2023 to 2025, 1.95% of revenue. The free cash flow above is struck after it and the valuation already charges the debt by subtracting net debt, so the charge falls by that much, from 12.10% to 10.14%. Restated at replacement capex: MRK spent $11,347mm on plant over 2023 to 2025 against $6,977mm of plant depreciation, 2.31% of revenue above what keeps the plant running. Taken at depreciation, the charge falls from 10.14% to 7.48%. Restated without one-off cash: MRK's free cash flow over 2023 to 2025 carried $8,300mm of deal payments in operating cash flow, capital allocation whose assets the book values separately; $572mm of legal settlements; $1,200mm of US transition tax (2025 instalment 1,200mm). None recurs, so the charge falls from 7.48% to 2.06%. Restated without working capital build: over 2023 to 2025 MRK's cash flow statement shows receivables up $2,482mm, inventories up $2,831mm, payables down $88mm, a working capital build of $5,401mm, 2.85% of revenue. Growth ties that cash up once, not on every product for ever, so the charge falls from 2.06% to -1.23%. Rebuilt on the book's own ratios on 0.3610 of the revenue they are struck on, against 0.3746 the filings leave as cash over 2023 to 2025 (free cash flow before interest, at replacement capex, without one-off cash and without working capital build), so the charge is -1.3576%.

new_note: do not also state untreated_carryover_pct 0. A convention, not a measurement: no US COPD incidence sits beside the prevalence
new_source: stated equal to the prevalence data/epidemiology.csv fills (14.2mm US adults with diagnosed COPD, BRFSS), as tozorakimab, AZD6793, GSK3862995B and lunsekimig do on this indication, which is the carryover-0 convention: the penetration is the share of each year's eligible patients started

new_note: a floor: the authors call it possibly an underestimate, since PH-COPD is rarely diagnosed and the cohort also required 12 months of enrolment before and 6 after the PH diagnosis. Screening studies find PH in 39.2% of COPD patients (Zhang L et al., Int J COPD 2022;17:1365-1379, meta-analysis), almost all undiagnosed. The other way, INSIGNIA-PH-COPD requires right heart catheterisation, which only 8.95% of claims-defined PH-COPD patients had (Weiss 2022, above), and excludes resting SpO2 below 88%
new_source: the claims-diagnosed PH-COPD share of US COPD patients: 'Of 273,792 patients with COPD identified, 2,224 ... were included in the PH-COPD cohort' (Weiss T et al., BMC Pulm Med 2023;23:455, doi:10.1186/s12890-023-02698-9, PMC10664271, Merck-funded; IQVIA PharMetrics Plus, October 2014 to May 2020). PH-COPD there is 1 inpatient or 2 outpatient PH diagnoses after a COPD diagnosis, with other PH groups, left heart failure, other chronic lung disease and cancer excluded. 2,224 / 273,792 = 0.8123%, about 115,346 of the 14.2mm

new_note: the 0.5 is a judgement and the most arguable figure here. For more: if approved it would be the first PH-COPD therapy, as Tyvaso was in PH-ILD; once-daily; pulmonary-selective, and in a Phase 1 in PH-COPD it improved pulmonary haemodynamics without systemic vasodilation (INSIGNIA-PH-COPD design abstract, Am J Respir Crit Care Med 2025;212(Suppl 1) A65-11, citing Bajwa et al., Int J COPD 2024); and Merck already sells Ohtuvayre in COPD. Against: PERFECT, inhaled treprostinil in PH-COPD, was stopped early because it raised serious adverse events with a suggestion of higher mortality (Nathan SD et al., Eur Respir J 2024;63:2400172), so prescribers will be wary of a vasodilator here; the Phase 2a result is unpublished five months after primary completion; and diagnosis needs a right heart catheter. The analogue's denominator is every PH-ILD patient seen over 3.5 years, larger than the pool at any one time, so its yearly rate reads low
new_source: ANCHOR, inhaled treprostinil in PH-ILD, the one Group 3 PH launch with a measured uptake. Cassady SJ et al., Pulm Circ 2025;15(4):e70203 (doi:10.1002/pul2.70203, PMC12598575, Optum Clinformatics, United Therapeutics authors), patient attrition table: over 31 March 2021 to 30 September 2024, the first 3.5 years of the PH-ILD label, 560 adults with PH and ILD claims, 6 months of enrolment and a month of follow-up started inhaled treprostinil, against 7,670 meeting the same criteria who were never treated with it (step 7). 560 / 8,230 = 6.804% started within the window. Solved through this seed's curve (k 1.52, midpoint 0.58): the curve reads 0.2928, 0.6544, 0.8965 and 0.9754 in years 0 to 3, so the window, years 0 to 2 and half of year 3, sums to 2.3314 and the anchor peak is 0.06804 / 2.3314 = 0.02919 a year. MULTIPLE 0.5, A JUDGEMENT: 0.5 x 0.02919 = 0.014593, about 1,683 US starts a year at peak on the 115,346 pool and a stock near 2,400 at 70.04% stopping
new_unit: share of each year's eligible patients

new_note: the inhaled Group 3 launch on file with a series from launch (June 2022, United Therapeutics FY2025 10-K), so year 0 is a part year. It mixes PAH and PH-ILD patients and switches from nebulised Tyvaso, which makes it faster than a new-molecule launch into an untreated disease
new_source: fitted to Tyvaso DPI's CMS Part D launch, converted to new starts at this seed's stopping: beneficiaries 1,141, 3,017 and 4,385 over 2022 to 2024 (drug_demand) and 5,268 in 2025 (quarterly companion 4ff7c618-4e40-483a-b390-c8a58c94fa15), so starts are 1,141, 3,017 - 1,141 x 0.2996 = 2,675, 3,481 and 3,954. A least-squares logistic with a free plateau gives plateau 3,994, k 1.52, midpoint 0.58 years, root mean squared error 66.9 (1.7% of the plateau)
fitted with the midpoint above to Tyvaso DPI's Part D new starts

new_source: derived: Merck generated $39,599mm of free cash flow on $189,294mm of revenue over 2023, 2024 and 2025, a 20.92% margin, against the 29.5% its cost of sales, SG&A and R&D leave. Restated without working capital build: over 2023 to 2025 MRK's cash flow statement shows receivables up $2,482mm, inventories up $2,831mm, payables down $88mm, a working capital build of $5,401mm, 2.85% of revenue. new_note: continuing therapy, capped at two years
new_source: R-DXd is given until progression for up to two years in both phase 3 trials on file (NCT07743164, NCT07776691)

new_note: a comparator, not a price this product has. Spending over beneficiaries counts patients treated for part of the year, so it sits below a full year of therapy
new_source: Enhertu, CMS Medicare Part B 2024: $581,465,185 over 8,410 beneficiaries, $69,140 a beneficiary. Enhertu is Daiichi Sankyo's DXd ADC on the same linker and payload, and the closest comparator on file

new_note: Medicaid rebates and 340B discounts sit outside ASP and are not taken off, so the net price leans high. The 50% the AZN seeds take is a retail Part D convention and does not fit a drug bought and billed under Part B; Merck's Keytruda seed takes no haircut at all
new_source: Social Security Act section 1847A: Medicare Part B pays 106% of average sales price, and ASP is already net of manufacturer discounts and rebates, so the manufacturer's price is the CMS figure divided by 1.06, which is 5.66% below it

new_note: a maintenance analogue in the same line, not this molecule
new_source: no median is published for R-DXd in either setting. PRIMA (Gonzalez-Martin et al., N Engl J Med 2019, doi:10.1056/NEJMoa1910962), first-line niraparib maintenance, reports a median progression-free survival of 13.8 months in the overall population. At a constant hazard 0.5^(12/13.8) = 54.7% are on therapy after a year and none after two, the cap in both R-DXd trials, so the stock turns over as though 1 / (1 + 0.547) = 64.6% stopped each year

new_note: no filing is stated in Merck's 10-K or 10-Qs. REJOICE-Ovarian01 (NCT06161025), Daiichi Sankyo's phase 2/3 in platinum-resistant disease with Breakthrough Therapy designation, has a primary completion of February 2028 on ClinicalTrials.gov but is not on the trials table for this asset, so it neither dates nor sizes this forecast
new_source: the earliest primary completion among this asset's phase 3 trials: REJOICE-Ovarian05 (NCT07743164), August 2031, plus the time to file and launch

new_note: for R-DXd Merck bears 75% of the first $2.0bn of research and development (same note), and owes up to $5.5bn of sales-based milestones; neither is charged here. Japan sits inside the ex-US multiple at half rather than a 5% royalty
new_source: Merck FY2025 10-K (0000310158-26-000063), Note 4, Daiichi Sankyo: the companies share research and development costs equally, Daiichi Sankyo records sales worldwide, and the companies equally share expenses as well as profits worldwide except Japan, where Daiichi Sankyo keeps exclusive rights and Merck receives a 5% sales-based royalty

new_source: derived: Merck generated $39,599mm of free cash flow on $189,294mm of revenue over 2023, 2024 and 2025, a 20.92% margin, against the 29.5% its cost of sales, SG&A and R&D leave. Solved so the modelled book reproduces that margin rather than assumed from one line's cost structure: the alliance rows carry no cost of sales and Animal Health carries its own, so a ratio taken off a single product does not reconcile the company. The window barely matters here, unlike Pfizer: the same aggregate is 21.9% over five years and 21.3% over every year on file. Restated before interest: MRK paid $3,700mm of interest inside operating cash flow over 2023 to 2025, 1.95% of revenue. The free cash flow above is struck after it and the valuation already charges the debt by subtracting net debt, so the charge falls by that much, from 12.10% to 10.14%. Restated at replacement capex: MRK spent $11,347mm on plant over 2023 to 2025 against $6,977mm of plant depreciation, 2.31% of revenue above what keeps the plant running. Taken at depreciation, the charge falls from 10.14% to 7.48%. Restated without one-off cash: MRK's free cash flow over 2023 to 2025 carried $8,300mm of deal payments in operating cash flow, capital allocation whose assets the book values separately; $572mm of legal settlements; $1,200mm of US transition tax (2025 instalment 1,200mm). None recurs, so the charge falls from 7.48% to 2.06%. Restated without working capital build: over 2023 to 2025 MRK's cash flow statement shows receivables up $2,482mm, inventories up $2,831mm, payables down $88mm, a working capital build of $5,401mm, 2.85% of revenue. Growth ties that cash up once, not on every product for ever, so the charge falls from 2.06% to -1.23%. Rebuilt on the book's own ratios on 0.3610 of the revenue they are struck on, against 0.3746 the filings leave as cash over 2023 to 2025 (free cash flow before interest, at replacement capex, without one-off cash and without working capital build), so the charge is -1.3576%.

new_source: the collaboration's asset P&L as the Merck model carries it, because Merck and Moderna share its costs and profits equally, so the asset has one cost structure: derived: Merck generated $39,599mm of free cash flow on $189,294mm of revenue over 2023, 2024 and 2025, a 20.92% margin, against the 29.5% its cost of sales, SG&A and R&D leave. Solved so the modelled book reproduces that margin rather than assumed from one line's cost structure: the alliance rows carry no cost of sales and Animal Health carries its own, so a ratio taken off a single product does not reconcile the company. Restated before interest: MRK paid $3,700mm of interest inside operating cash flow over 2023 to 2025, 1.95% of revenue. The free cash flow above is struck after it and the valuation already charges the debt by subtracting net debt, so the charge falls by that much, from 12.10% to 10.14%. Restated at replacement capex: MRK spent $11,347mm on plant over 2023 to 2025 against $6,977mm of plant depreciation, 2.31% of revenue above what keeps the plant running. Taken at depreciation, the charge falls from 10.14% to 7.48%. Restated without one-off cash: MRK's free cash flow over 2023 to 2025 carried $8,300mm of deal payments in operating cash flow, capital allocation whose assets the book values separately; $572mm of legal settlements; $1,200mm of US transition tax (2025 instalment 1,200mm). None recurs, so the charge falls from 7.48% to 2.06%. Restated without working capital build: over 2023 to 2025 MRK's cash flow statement shows receivables up $2,482mm, inventories up $2,831mm, payables down $88mm, a working capital build of $5,401mm, 2.85% of revenue. Growth ties that cash up once, not on every product for ever, so the charge falls from 2.06% to -1.23%. Rebuilt on the book's own ratios on 0.3610 of the revenue they are struck on, against 0.3746 the filings leave as cash over 2023 to 2025 (free cash flow before interest, at replacement capex, without one-off cash and without working capital build), so the charge is -1.3576%.

The free cash flow above is struck after it and the valuation already charges the debt by subtracting net debt, so the charge falls by that much, from 29.59% to 29.04%. Restated at replacement capex: NVO spent 133,110mm DKK on plant over 2023 to 2025 against 19,625mm DKK of plant depreciation, 13.64% of revenue above what keeps the plant running. Taken at depreciation, the charge falls from 29.04% to 11.89%. Restated with selling costs: SG&A now carries NVO's filed selling or distribution costs, 20.81% of revenue this charge was absorbing, so it falls from 11.89% to nil. The filed lines alone now leave less than the cash the company made before interest and at replacement capex, and a charge below nil would credit the book with cash its own costs do not leave. Checked without one-off cash: deal payments are booked under investing, so free cash flow never carried them, and no settlement or transition tax is stated for the window, so the charge stands. Restated to the amortisation floor: the filed cost lines leave a 41.40% pre-tax margin where the cash over 2023 to 2025 supports 50.32%, so the charge rebuilds at -8.92%. It was held at nil, but NVO books 6,529mm DKK of non-cash amortisation of acquired intangibles inside its cost lines in FY2025 (0000353278-26-000012), 2.11% of revenue, so the charge stops at that floor: -2.11%. Restated without working capital build: over 2023 to 2025 NVO's cash flow statement shows receivables up 20,296mm DKK, inventories up 25,235mm DKK, payables up 15,158mm DKK, a working capital build of 30,373mm DKK, 3.65% of revenue. LV hypertrophy on exactly that threshold was present in 52% of the TOPCAT echocardiographic study (456 of the 875 of its 935 heart failure patients with a measurable LV mass index), 43% concentric and 9% eccentric, read by a core laboratory, 52% of them enrolled in the US (Shah AM et al., Circ Heart Fail 2014;7(1):104-115, doi:10.1161/CIRCHEARTFAILURE.113.000887, PMID 24249049, PMC4467731). Applied to the whole pool, both ejection fraction halves: for the reduced half it is a floor, because LV mass index runs higher in reduced than in preserved ejection fraction (118 against 98 g/m2 among 831 consecutive heart failure outpatients, ESC Heart Fail 2021, doi:10.1002/ehf2.13366, PMID 34085774, PMC8318400) and that trial also admits dilatation without hypertrophy. 0.52 x 7.4mm = about 3.85mm

Checked at replacement capex: no plant depreciation on file for every year, and no amortisation line to take it out of the combined figure, so the charge stands. US net revenue: $10mm in 2024 and $155mm in 2025 (BMY 10-K 0000014272-26-000004, where non-US is nil), and $240mm for 2026 (Q2 US $60mm x4, 8-K exhibit 0000014272-26-000018). Net per patient = 0.5 x $6,986.06 = $3,493.03. Stock: 2,863, 44,374 and 68,708. At this file's 59.26% stopping, 40.74% remain, so new starts are 2,863, 43,208 = 44,374 - 2,863 x 0.4074, and 50,632 = 68,708 - 44,374 x 0.4074. The pool is 1,200,448 less cumulative starts: 1,197,585 in 2025 and 1,154,377 in 2026. Capture: 3.608% in 2025 and 4.386% in 2026, which is the anchor. Benlysta (belimumab) CMS Medicare Part D 2025, from the quarterly companion 4ff7c618 (Q1-Q4 2025): $291,468,828 over 7,431 beneficiaries = $39,223.37 per beneficiary. Why this comparator: no systemic Sjögren's therapy is marketed in the US, and Novartis itself calls ianalumab the potential first targeted treatment. Benlysta is the closest marketed match. It acts on the same BAFF pathway (it targets the ligand, ianalumab the receptor). It is prescribed by rheumatologists for SLE, the neighbouring systemic autoimmune disease. Its subcutaneous form is self-injected on the pharmacy benefit, as monthly 300 mg subcutaneous ianalumab will be (NCT06293365 tests its 2 mL autoinjector). The 2024 annual Part D figure was $37,182. Alternative: Benlysta Part B at $36,043.10 per beneficiary with a 0.056604 discount gives a net of $34,003, 73% above this net. Benlysta's mature per-beneficiary figure is used as is, not annualised.
