Maciel G et al., Arthritis Care Res 2017;69:1612-1616 (doi 10.1002/acr.23173, PMC5478481), Olmsted County prevalent cohort on 1 Jan 2015: 9 of 106 with moderate (ESSDAI 5-13) and 7 with high (≥14) systemic activity, so 16/106 = 15.09% meet the ESSDAI ≥5 bar NEPTUNUS-1 and -2 enrolled. This is a floor. The authors warn that retrospective chart scoring under-counts the biological domain. The same group's incident cohort had 29.5% (18/61) at diagnosis (Maciel, Mayo Clin Proc 2017). NEPTUNUS also required diagnosis within 7.5 years and anti-Ro/SSA positivity, which the label may or may not carry. It MUST equal dazodalibep's value exactly: pool_crowding pools only claimants with the same prevalence x eligible_pct.

Capture identity from backend/capture_anchor.py (untreated convention), applied to Saphnelo, the last new biologic mechanism launched into a systemic autoimmune rheumatic disease. Saphnelo US revenue was $8m, $111m, $260m, $425m and $596m in 2021 to 2025 (AZ 20-F 0001104659-24-025553 and 0001104659-26-019130). The net price is $35,856 per patient-year (CMS Part B 2025: $38,007.17 per beneficiary x 1/1.06). That gives treated stocks of 223, 3,096, 7,251, 11,853 and 16,622. After 45.54% stop each year, new starts are 2,974, 5,565, 7,904 and 10,167. Against the untreated CDC SLE pool of 204,295, that is 1.46%, 2.77%, 4.04% and 5.42% (5.04% under the engine pool convention). 2025 is Saphnelo's fourth full year, which is 51.9% of the way up the fitted curve (k 0.31, midpoint 2.76). So the engine needs 10.45% to reproduce 5.42% at the same point. JUDGEMENT: multiple 0.75, giving 0.0784, which converts 4.07% of the untreated eligible pool in ianalumab's fourth year. Case for a higher multiple: it would be the first and only targeted Sjögren's therapy, while Saphnelo launched beside Benlysta. It is a monthly self-injection, not an IV. Two Phase 3s were positive and it has Breakthrough designation. The anchor is measured against all diagnosed SLE patients, not Saphnelo's narrower label pool, so it leans low. Case against: the placebo-adjusted ESSDAI gain was only -1.3 (NEPTUNUS-1, p=0.0496) and -1.0 (NEPTUNUS-2 monthly, p=0.041). The every-3-months arm failed (-0.5, p=0.34), and pooled patient-reported secondaries missed significance. ESSDAI must be scored for payers, and Maciel 2017 found community rheumatologists rarely run those tests. Crowded pool: dazodalibep follows in 2029, and nipocalimab (JNJ), deucravacitinib (BMY), telitacicept (VOR) and efgartigimod (argenx, readout July 2027) all have Sjögren's Phase 3s. None of them carries rows on indication 85 today. Pool crowding: pool_crowding.solve on indication:85 with dazodalibep rations no year (combined starts peak at 11.7% of the eligible pool). Counting the population once trims ianalumab's peak starts to 0.9348 of its standalone run.

Restated before interest: NVS paid $2,587mm of interest inside operating cash flow over 2023 to 2025, 1.72% of revenue. The free cash flow above is struck after it and the valuation already charges the debt by subtracting net debt, so adding it back only widens a gap the filed lines already leave, and the charge stays nil. Checked at replacement capex: no plant depreciation on file for every year, and no amortisation line to take it out of the combined figure, so the charge stands. Checked without one-off cash: deal payments are booked under investing, so free cash flow never carried them, and no settlement or transition tax is stated for the window, so the charge stands. Restated to the amortisation floor: the filed cost lines leave a 30.05% pre-tax margin where the cash over 2023 to 2025 supports 37.20%, so the charge rebuilds at -7.15%. It was held at nil, but NVS books $3,197mm of non-cash amortisation of acquired intangibles inside its cost lines in FY2025 (0001114448-26-000004), 5.86% of revenue, so the charge stops at that floor: -5.86%. Restated without working capital build: over 2023 to 2025 NVS's cash flow statement shows receivables up $3,559mm, inventories up $737mm, payables up $101mm, a working capital build of $4,195mm, 2.79% of revenue. Growth ties that cash up once, not on every product for ever, so the charge was held at the amortisation floor, -5.86% where the filed figures rebuild it at -7.15%, and stays there. Struck on total revenue: Novartis's filed cost lines sit against net sales of USD 54,532mm and other revenues of USD 2,142mm together (FY2025 20-F 0001114448-26-000004, Note 4), and the income statement shows other revenues above cost of goods sold with no cost of their own, so each ratio is scaled by 54,532 over 56,674 and charged on every revenue the model carries. The book's costs are the filed ones either way; this shares them across the revenue that earned them. Rebuilt on the book's own ratios on 0.3269 of the revenue they are struck on, against 0.3911 the filings leave as cash over 2023 to 2025 (free cash flow before interest, at replacement capex, without one-off cash and without working capital build), so the charge is -5.8626%.

new_source: No progression-free survival exists for JSB462 with Pluvicto until NCT07047118 reads out, so this uses its control arm. In PSMAfore, taxane-naive PSMA-positive mCRPC after one ARPI, Pluvicto's median radiographic progression-free survival was 11.60 months at the third data cutoff, median follow-up 24.11 months (Morris et al., Lancet 2024;404:1227-39, doi:10.1016/S0140-6736(24)01653-2, PubMed abstract). JSB462 is taken daily until progression, so at a constant hazard 0.5^(12/11.60) = 48.82% remain after a year and 51.18% stop

new_source: the post-ARPI pool mrk_opevesostat.csv and jnj_jnj_101556143.csv carry, with both sources re-opened. 11.5% of diagnoses reach mCRPC: 'annual incidence was about 36,100 in the United States' (Su, Wu and Shi, Front Pharmacol 2021, doi:10.3389/fphar.2020.610601, citing Scher et al. 2015) against 313,780. Narrowed to the 42.6% treated after an ARPI: among 6,301 US mCRPC patients diagnosed 2018 to 2023 (Flatiron; Efstathiou et al., J Clin Oncol 2025;43(5 suppl):74), 78% received a line of therapy, 29% were ARPI-experienced before mCRPC, 75% of first lines were an ARPI and 48% of treated patients reached a second line: 0.78 x (0.29 + 0.71 x 0.75 x 0.48) = 42.6%, and 0.115 x 0.426 = 0.0489

new_note: The case for more: Pluvicto is also taken later, 23 of 89 third-line starts (25.8%) in the 2024 cohort, and across all lines of the 2021 to 2025 cohorts Lu-177 was started 723 times (113, 187, 215, 137 and 71 from first to fifth line) against about 2,600 men who reached a line after an ARPI (705 ARPI-experienced at first line, plus 3,541 ARPI-naive men started on an ARPI of whom the cohort's 53.6% reached a second line), roughly 28%; Pluvicto's pre-taxane label (efficacy supplement approved 2025-03-28, NDA215833) postdates most of that follow-up. The case for less: an add-on reaches only part of its partner's patients, the combination must beat Pluvicto alone (primary endpoint PSA50), Pluvicto's label now carries PSMA-positive hormone-sensitive disease in combination with an ARPI (efficacy supplement 37 approved 2026-07-31, NDA215833, openFDA; label effective 2026-08-12), which moves some of its use out of this line, and opevesostat, ifinatamab deruxtecan and JNJ-101556143 claim the same pool
new_source: ANCHOR, a measured share of the line. JSB462's lead use is added to Pluvicto (NCT07047118), so the patients it can reach are the ones who take Pluvicto. Among US mCRPC patients who started first-line therapy in 2024 (Flatiron, about 280 mostly community centres), Lu-177 was 47 of 344 second-line starts, 13.7% (Hooper et al., JAMA Netw Open 2026;9(6):e2620750, doi:10.1001/jamanetworkopen.2026.20750, PMC13316606), up from 18 of 894 (2.0%) in the 2021 cohort. Second line is the first line after an ARPI for most of the pool: 4,041 of 5,096 first lines (79.3%) across the 2021 to 2025 cohorts were an ARPI. So the base case gives JSB462 every Pluvicto patient in the line it is tested in. No independent peak forecast for JSB462 or ARV-766 was found: Novartis and Arvinas give none, and a search of analyst coverage found none

new_source: derived and found to be nil: NVS's filed expense lines already leave less than the 31.44% of revenue it turned into free cash over 2023 to 2025, so there is nothing left to charge. Restated before interest: NVS paid $2,587mm of interest inside operating cash flow over 2023 to 2025, 1.72% of revenue. The free cash flow above is struck after it and the valuation already charges the debt by subtracting net debt, so adding it back only widens a gap the filed lines already leave, and the charge stays nil. Checked at replacement capex: no plant depreciation on file for every year, and no amortisation line to take it out of the combined figure, so the charge stands. Checked without one-off cash: deal payments are booked under investing, so free cash flow never carried them, and no settlement or transition tax is stated for the window, so the charge stands. Restated to the amortisation floor: the filed cost lines leave a 30.05% pre-tax margin where the cash over 2023 to 2025 supports 37.20%, so the charge rebuilds at -7.15%. It was held at nil, but NVS books $3,197mm of non-cash amortisation of acquired intangibles inside its cost lines in FY2025 (0001114448-26-000004), 5.86% of revenue, so the charge stops at that floor: -5.86%. Restated without working capital build: over 2023 to 2025 NVS's cash flow statement shows receivables up $3,559mm, inventories up $737mm, payables up $101mm, a working capital build of $4,195mm, 2.79% of revenue. Growth ties that cash up once, not on every product for ever, so the charge was held at the amortisation floor, -5.86% where the filed figures rebuild it at -7.15%, and stays there. Struck on total revenue: Novartis's filed cost lines sit against net sales of USD 54,532mm and other revenues of USD 2,142mm together (FY2025 20-F 0001114448-26-000004, Note 4), and the income statement shows other revenues above cost of goods sold with no cost of their own, so each ratio is scaled by 54,532 over 56,674 and charged on every revenue the model carries. The book's costs are the filed ones either way; this shares them across the revenue that earned them. Rebuilt on the book's own ratios on 0.3269 of the revenue they are struck on, against 0.3911 the filings leave as cash over 2023 to 2025 (free cash flow before interest, at replacement capex, without one-off cash and without working capital build), so the charge is -5.8626%.

new_note: Taken continuously until it stops working or is not tolerated
new_source: MANIFEST-2 design (PMID 40065169, doi:10.1038/s41591-025-03572-3): pelabresib 125 mg once daily, 14 days on and 7 off, with ruxolitinib, given continuously; about half of patients were still on assigned treatment at a median follow-up of 115.9 weeks (48.6% against 48.1%, ASH 2025, Blood 2025;146 suppl 1:910)

new_note: Judgement on the comparator, house convention: ruxolitinib is the backbone pelabresib is added to and the control arm of both Phase 3s, so it is the closest marketed drug in the same disease and line. Alternatives from the same 2025 file: Ojjaara $177,155.96 a beneficiary (3,090), Inrebic $135,541.93 (361), Vonjo $111,684.16 (1,153). Case against: an add-on doubles the regimen cost payers see, and Jakafi's figure mixes in PV and GvHD use. Not annualised: the per-beneficiary basis measured at a median 96% of CMS negotiated prices (backend/gross_to_net.py). No list price for pelabresib exists
new_source: Jakafi (ruxolitinib), CMS Medicare Part D 2025, from the quarterly companion 4ff7c618-4e40-483a-b390-c8a58c94fa15, row '2025 (Q1-Q4)', manufacturer 'Overall': $2,342,281,748.71 over 17,288 beneficiaries = $135,485.99 a beneficiary. Jakafi has one presentation. The 2024 annual figure was $132,549 (drug_demand, 15,713 beneficiaries); 2025 is used because it exists

new_note: Direction checked: 0.5 off list, so net is 0.135486 x 0.5 = $67,743 per patient-year
new_source: house convention on a CMS Part D per-beneficiary price (halving lands at a median 96% of CMS negotiated net prices; backend/gross_to_net.py)

new_note: Constant hazard: 1 - 0.565^(52.18/96) = 0.2668 per year. Case for higher: stops for adverse events were 21.0% on the combination against 13.4% on ruxolitinib alone, and trial retention usually beats real-world retention. Case for lower: the placebo arm completed at a similar 59.3%, so most stopping is disease-driven rather than drug-driven
new_source: MANIFEST-2 96-week analysis (Rampal et al., ASH 2025, Blood 2025;146 suppl 1:910, doi:10.1182/blood-2025-910): 56.5% (121 of 214) of the pelabresib-ruxolitinib arm completed 96 weeks of assigned treatment
new_unit: share of treated stock stopping per year

new_note: Novartis lists a first planned submission of 2026 for DAK539 in myelofibrosis and gives no US date (Q2 2026 6-K 0001114448-26-000012, pipeline table). That submission is the EU one on MANIFEST-2's 96-week data, so ex-US sales could start about two years before 2030; the engine runs one start year per asset and this seed takes the US one. MANIFEST-2's own primary completion (2023-08-23) does not gate the US filing and is not used
new_source: NCT07357727 (MANIFEST-3), ClinicalTrials.gov API, last update 2026-09-25: primary completion 2028-05-17 (estimated), plus two calendar years, the book's first-full-year convention. It is the trial the US filing waits on: in January 2026 Novartis announced an EU filing in 2026 and a new Phase 3 in the United States, Canada and Japan (Royalty Pharma FY2025 10-K 0001802768-26-000003); ApexOnco (2026-01-26) reports MANIFEST-3 as the study that supports the US filing

new_note: A flat 3%, so there is no tier to choose. Recompute if Novartis's cost rows change. The 0.97 first written took the royalty off revenue rather than off margin. Constellation's agreement with the Leukemia & Lymphoma Society carries up to $25mm of capped payments on licensing, change of control or approval, not a royalty on sales (Constellation FY2020 10-K 0001564590-21-007783), and this book does not net milestones. No co-commercialisation partner
new_source: Royalty Pharma 8-K, June 2021 (0001193125-21-179284, ex. 99.1): as part of its funding of MorphoSys's purchase of Constellation, Royalty Pharma bought the right to 3% of future net sales of pelabresib; its FY2025 10-K (0001802768-26-000003) still lists pelabresib. Novartis owns MorphoSys outright after the 2024 acquisition. Netted as the book nets every royalty, over Novartis's pre-tax margin from its own cost rows in this file: 1 - 0.241706 - 0.23372 - 0.197637 + 0.058626 = 0.385563, so 1 - 0.03 / 0.385563 = 0.922192

new_note: Judgement. The whole-disease count is 21,133 US patients in 2023, 6.3 per 100,000 (Masarova et al., J Clin Oncol 2025;43(16 suppl):e18575, Optum Research Database standardised to the 2023 US population). Most of them are already on a JAK inhibitor. Case against: a JAK inhibitor is often started well after diagnosis, so some prevalent untreated patients are still eligible and this pool understates the early years
new_source: Set equal to incidence: pelabresib is a first-line add-on for JAK inhibitor-naive patients, a line of therapy, so the book's convention states prevalence equal to incidence and the engine carries no untreated patients over. Myelofibrosis is not in data/epidemiology.csv and no other seed carries a myelofibrosis pool (bomedemstat leaves it out)

new_note: The study identifies MF by ICD-10 D75.81 or D47.4, so it covers primary, post-PV and post-ET myelofibrosis, all of which MANIFEST-2 and MANIFEST-3 enrol
new_source: US myelofibrosis incidence of 1.56 per 100,000 person-years in 2023 against a prevalence of 6.3 per 100,000 (Gerds et al., Blood 2025;146 suppl 1:5576, doi:10.1182/blood-2025-5576, Optum Research Database standardised by age, sex and region to 2023 US census data). The companion abstract counts that prevalence as 21,133 patients (J Clin Oncol 2025;43(16 suppl):e18575). 21,133 x 1.56 / 6.3 = 5,233

new_note: Judgement: applies only the platelet filter. MANIFEST-3 also requires DIPSS intermediate-1 or higher, a spleen of at least 450 cm3, a mean total symptom score of at least 15 and no prior JAK or BET inhibitor. No source gives the combined share, so the pool overstates the label
new_source: Platelets of at least 100 x 10^9/L, an entry criterion of MANIFEST-3 (NCT07357727, registry eligibility) and of the MANIFEST-2 population. Up to a quarter of MF patients have platelets below 100,000 at presentation (Yilmaz and Verstovsek, Expert Rev Hematol 2022;15(3):233, PMID 35316110). At this file's 50.30% stopping, 49.70% remain, so 2025 new starts are 105,939 - 105,539 x 0.4970 = 53,487. The pool is 10,550,000 x 0.70 = 7,385,000 eligible, less the 105,539 on Multaq, plus 700,000 eligible diagnoses (1,000,000 x 0.70) = 7,979,461. Rebuilt on the book's own ratios on 0.3269 of the revenue they are struck on, against 0.3911 the filings leave as cash over 2023 to 2025 (free cash flow before interest, at replacement capex, without one-off cash and without working capital build), so the charge is -5.8626%.

new_note: JUDGEMENT. Cross-check: a pilot definition of severe refractory SLE (SLEDAI-2K of 10 or more despite glucocorticoids and immunosuppressants at two visits) caught 578 of 3,744 patients, 14% (Kandane-Rathnayake R et al., Arthritis Res Ther 2025, doi 10.1186/s13075-025-03622-8; 13 Asia-Pacific countries). Pushing lower: a change of sequence can follow intolerance or non-persistence rather than an inadequate response, and the trial's SLEDAI-2K of 6 or more, age 18 to 75 and organ function criteria are not taken off. Pushing higher: Masurkar's cohort is newly diagnosed and followed about four years, so the share of the prevalent stock ever past two lines is larger
new_source: Two shares multiplied. (1) Past two lines: of 2,476 US adults with incident SLE who started treatment, 418 (16.882%) reached a third sequence of therapy, a new sequence being a different SLE drug added or switched to more than 30 days after the last, over a mean 47.8 months' follow-up (Masurkar PP et al., Lupus Sci Med 2024;11(2), doi 10.1136/lupus-2024-001290, PMC11683911; MarketScan commercial and Medicare supplemental, first diagnosis 2013 to 2017). AUTOGRAPH requires an inadequate response to at least two therapies. (2) On treatment: 5,360 of 5,984 US adults with SLE (89.572%) filled an SLE medication in 2023 (Figueroa-Parra G et al., Lupus Sci Med 2024;11(2), PMC11629018; OptumLabs). 0.16882 x 0.89572 = 0.151216, about 30,890 US patients and 2,157 newly eligible a year

new_note: JUDGEMENT, the BMS-986353 method with the exit read from the pool rather than a survival study. Deaths alone are fewer: 401 of 1,353 prevalent patients in the Georgia Lupus Registry died from 2002 through 2016 (Lim SS et al., MMWR 2019;68:419-422), about 2.4% a year at a constant rate over 14.5 years, which would give 0.976 and let the eligible pool grow to about three times its size. The long-run count of infusions is the same either way, the lifetime share times the inflow; only the draw on the prevalent stock is faster here. Not a line of cancer therapy, so it is not 0

new_note: JUDGEMENT: a multiple of 1.0 on the second-line share, the book's autoimmune CAR-T convention. The third-line 36% matches AUTOGRAPH's two failed therapies by line, but a lupus patient after two lines still has Benlysta, Saphnelo and, in nephritis, Gazyva to try, where a third-line lymphoma patient does not, so the lower share is taken. Case for lower: three deaths from IEC-HS halted the programme in August 2026 and will make rheumatologists cautious; rese-cel, zola-cel and T-cell engagers will compete for the same patients; the lymphoma denominator is fit patients only. Case for higher: lupus patients are younger, and a drug-free remission after one infusion appeals against lifelong immunosuppression. Cross-check, not solved to: GlobalData's model had rap-cel at $32mm of US revenue in 2038 across lymphoma and lupus (Pharmaceutical Technology, updated 27 August 2024), a single year from before the Phase 2 lupus programme and not stated as a peak or as unrisked
new_source: Perales MA et al., 'Real-world treatment patterns of patients with large B-cell lymphoma over time and into a post-CAR T approval era', Blood Adv 2026, doi 10.1182/bloodadvances.2025019064 (Flatiron): among patients deemed eligible and fit for CAR-T, 25% received it in second line and 36% in third line. Read as a lifetime share, as BMS-986353 does, and solved through the engine's identity so a patient in the eligible pool has a 25% chance of being infused before leaving it: p / (1 - (1 - p) x 0.930184) = 0.25, so p = 0.25 x 0.069816 / (1 - 0.25 x 0.930184) = 0.022743

new_source: JUDGEMENT. NCT07094516 completes 2028-09-14 (ClinicalTrials.gov, updated 2026-06-26), no Phase 3 is registered, and Novartis gives first submission as 2029 or later (FY2025 20-F, Q2 2026 6-K). Novartis's own gap from a Phase 2b completion to a Phase 3 start is remibrutinib's 10.5 months (NCT03926611 completed 2021-01-14, NCT05030311 started 2021-11-30), so a Phase 3 starts about July 2029. Kisunla went from its Phase 3 start (TRAILBLAZER-ALZ 2, NCT04437511, 2020-06-19) to its first full year, 2025, in 4.53 years, and Leqembi from Clarity AD (NCT03887455, 2019-03-27) to 2024 in 4.77 years (the intervals mrk_mk_2214.csv records). July 2029 plus 4.5 to 4.8 years reaches February to May 2034, so the first full year on sale is 2035

new_note: wholly owned; no licence, partner or royalty found
new_source: Novartis's FY2025 20-F selected development projects table lists VHB937, a TREM2 stabilizer and activator, in Alzheimer's disease and ALS under footnote 1 only, a project added to the table in 2025 on entering confirmatory development, where acquired projects carry their own footnote (abelacimab 'following the acquisition of Anthos Therapeutics in 2025', pacibekitug 'following the acquisition of Tourmaline Bio in 2025'). new_note: NCT07094516 enrols the same stage, MCI due to AD or mild AD with CDR 0.5 or 1 and AD confirmed by CSF or amyloid PET. Not a true share: the numerator includes MCI, which the 7.4mm excludes. It must equal the other claimants' for the pool to hold
new_source: a scaling to a sourced absolute label pool, the one trontinemab, BMS-986446 and MK-2214 carry: about 2.2 million US residents could be eligible for lecanemab, amyloid-positive with MCI or mild dementia (Dittrich A et al., Neurology 2024;102(9):e209402), over the 7,400,000 aged 65 and over with Alzheimer's dementia that data/epidemiology.csv carries. 2.2 / 7.4 = 0.297

new_note: the 0.5 is the most arguable figure here. For more: a new mechanism acting on microglia rather than on amyloid or tau, with a clinical primary endpoint in its Phase 2, and TREM2 is better validated in Alzheimer's than ALS (Guggenheim, reported by European Biotechnology). Against: the first TREM2 agonist antibody, Alector's AL002, 'failed to meet the primary endpoint' of CDR-SB in INVOKE-2 (Alector release, 2024-11-25); VHB937 itself missed both endpoints in ALS; it is a further infusion beside anti-amyloid therapy; and it would launch about 2035 behind subcutaneous and brain-shuttle antibodies
new_source: ANCHOR, the measured anti-amyloid class new-start rate from CMS Part B beneficiaries, queried 2026-09-28. Leqembi (J0174): 961 in 2023 and 7,907 in 2024 (Medicare Part B Spending by Drug, dataset 76a714ad-3a2c-43ac-b76d-9dadf8f7d890) and 14,029 in 2025 (quarterly file bf6a5b3b-31ee-4abb-b1ad-2607a1e7510a, row '2025 (Q1-Q4)'). Kisunla (J0175): 1,299 in 2024 (drug_demand) and 9,993 in 2025 (quarterly file). At this seed's stopping of 0.724702, 27.53% of a year's patients carry into the next, so 2025 new starts are 14,029 - 7,907 x 0.2753 = 11,852 and 9,993 - 1,299 x 0.2753 = 9,635, 21,488 together. A year's eligible pool in the engine's terms is the carried pool plus the inflow, in the first year 2,197,800 + 270,270 = 2,468,070, so the class started 0.8706% of it in 2025. MULTIPLE 0.5, A JUDGEMENT: 0.5 x 0.8706% = 0.4353%, the multiple MK-2214 and BMS-986446 take
new_unit: share of the eligible untreated pool started per year

new_source: The comparator is Voyxact (sibeprenlimab), Otsuka's anti-APRIL antibody for IgAN, approved 25 November 2025. It is self-injected every 4 weeks (openFDA label, effective 2026-03-17: 400 mg once every 4 weeks, one single-dose syringe per carton), so it matches zigakibart on class, disease and care setting. The source is CMS Medicare Quarterly Part D Spending by Drug (dataset 4ff7c618-4e40-483a-b390-c8a58c94fa15), 2026 Q1, still the latest quarter carrying Voyxact: $4,640,340.95 over 151 claims is $30,730.73 a claim, and 13 four-week doses a year gives $399,499.49. This uses the launch-year exception, not the per-beneficiary default. Voyxact's Q1 2026 per-beneficiary figure is $51,559.34: its 90 beneficiaries took 1.68 claims each, out of a 13-dose year, so that figure is a part-year artefact and not a price. It is the same class price povetacicept carries, and sefaxersen carries it converted to CHF. Alternatives: the published WAC of about $390,000 a year (ICER, B-Cell Directed Therapies for IgAN, 2026), which the per-claim figure sits 2.4% above; Trutakna (atacicept) at about $425,000 per the povetacicept seed (not re-verified here); Fabhalta at a 2026 Q1 Part D $47,568.79 a claim (monthly fill), about $570,800 a year, as the upside case. Zigakibart doses every 2 weeks (600 mg SC, per BEYOND), but the price is a class price per patient-year, so its dose count does not multiply it.

new_note: the 0.5 multiple is a judgement; pool_crowding keeps zigakibart at 92.6% of its uncrowded peak beside povetacicept and sefaxersen
new_source: This is the Filspari anchor times 0.5, and the 0.5 is a labelled judgement. I reproduced the capture_anchor identity myself. Filspari US net sales were $29.208mm (2023), $132.222mm (2024) and $322.005mm (2025), from Travere 8-K exhibits 99.1, 0001438533-25-000008 and 0001438533-26-000013. Its CMS Part D 2025 Q1-Q4 figure is $61,544,556.93 over 4,761 claims, or $12,926.81 a 30-tablet claim, which is $157,276.19 a year. That makes stocks of 185.7, 840.7 and 2,047.4 patients. Net of 27.5% stopping each year, new starts are 185.7, 706.1 and 1,437.9. Over the untreated eligible pool (198,887 x 0.6851 = 136,257.5, less prior starts) that is a capture of 0.136%, 0.519% and 1.062% (1.026% on the engine's pool plus incidence). Run through the engine itself (forecast.derive_new_patients and treated_stock, midpoint 1.7, k 1.32), it needs a peak of 0.01617 to reach 2,047.4 patients in year 3. The engine path tracks 219, 828 and 2,047 against the filed 186, 841 and 2,047. That is the 0.0162 povetacicept carries. The 2,047 is a floor, because the stock is divided by a gross price. The multiple of 0.5 gives 0.0081, the same as sefaxersen. Case for going lower: zigakibart is the fourth B-cell entrant. It arrives about 3 years after Voyxact (Nov 2025) and about 2.5 years after Trutakna (Jul 2026) and povetacicept (PDUFA 30 Nov 2026). It doses twice as often as Voyxact and povetacicept. ICER issued an access and affordability alert at $292,500 net: only 6% of eligible patients fit its $821mm budget threshold. Novartis's own Fabhalta and Vanrafia treat the same patients. Case for going higher: Novartis already has a nephrology field force through Fabhalta and Vanrafia, and BEYOND's primary endpoint is eGFR at week 104, which could support full approval where its peers launched on accelerated approval. Cross-check, also a judgement: if the class runs at about 3x Filspari's pace (the povetacicept seed's reading of Voyxact's 90 Q1 2026 beneficiaries) and is split by the order-of-entry penalty of Urban et al., Management Science 1986 (share ratio of about entry order^-0.49), a fourth entrant gets 0.507/2.80 x 3 = 0.54x Filspari, close to the 0.5 chosen. Re-solved 2026-10-05 after untreated patients were given an exit (carryover P/(P+I)): the same target now needs 0.00853856, was 0.0081 (the anchor path, now at carryover 0.9661, solves to 0.0170771, was 0.0161748, times the multiple of 0.5).

new_source: This is the book's own fit to Tarpeyo, the first IgAN-specific launch, carried so that all three IgAN claimants share one curve. Tarpeyo's CMS Part D beneficiaries were 52 (2022), 247 (2023) and 468 (2024) in the annual file (7e0b4365-fd63-4a29-8f5e-e0ac9f66a81b), and 680 in 2025 Q1-Q4 in the quarterly file. The book fits k 1.32, midpoint 1.70, rmse 17. My independent least-squares refit gives k 1.36, midpoint 1.67, rmse 16.5, the same shape on a flat error surface. Filspari (112, 323, 660 over 2023 to 2025) fits k 1.30, midpoint 1.66, but three points for three parameters is exact, so it describes the curve rather than testing it. The midpoint is measured from forecast_start_year, with no offset. Caveat: Tarpeyo is a nine-month course whose beneficiaries turn over, and the fit ignores that.

The 2021 and 2022 COVID years are excluded because a 36% margin on a vaccine windfall is not what this company earns. Restated before interest: PFE paid $8,181mm of interest inside operating cash flow over 2023 to 2025, 4.40% of revenue. The free cash flow above is struck after it and the valuation already charges the debt by subtracting net debt, so the charge falls by that much, from 22.18% to 17.77%. Checked at replacement capex: no plant depreciation on file for every year, and no amortisation line to take it out of the combined figure, so the charge stands. Restated without one-off cash: PFE's free cash flow over 2023 to 2025 carried $1,350mm of deal payments in operating cash flow, capital allocation whose assets the book values separately; $63mm of legal settlements; $4,400mm of US transition tax (2023 instalment 1,000mm; 2024 instalment 1,300mm; 2025 instalment 2,100mm). None recurs, so the charge falls from 17.77% to 14.52%. Restated without working capital build: over 2023 to 2025 PFE's cash flow statement shows receivables up $25mm, inventories up $1,462mm, payables down $1,792mm, a working capital build of $3,279mm, 1.77% of revenue. Growth ties that cash up once, not on every product for ever, so the charge falls from 14.52% to 12.66%.

The 2021 and 2022 COVID years are excluded because a 36% margin on a vaccine windfall is not what this company earns. Restated before interest: PFE paid $8,181mm of interest inside operating cash flow over 2023 to 2025, 4.40% of revenue. The free cash flow above is struck after it and the valuation already charges the debt by subtracting net debt, so the charge falls by that much, from 22.18% to 17.77%. Checked at replacement capex: no plant depreciation on file for every year, and no amortisation line to take it out of the combined figure, so the charge stands. Restated without one-off cash: PFE's free cash flow over 2023 to 2025 carried $1,350mm of deal payments in operating cash flow, capital allocation whose assets the book values separately; $63mm of legal settlements; $4,400mm of US transition tax (2023 instalment 1,000mm; 2024 instalment 1,300mm; 2025 instalment 2,100mm). None recurs, so the charge falls from 17.77% to 14.52%. Restated without working capital build: over 2023 to 2025 PFE's cash flow statement shows receivables up $25mm, inventories up $1,462mm, payables down $1,792mm, a working capital build of $3,279mm, 1.77% of revenue. Growth ties that cash up once, not on every product for ever, so the charge falls from 14.52% to 12.66%.

new_source: One rate weighted across the two lines by their eligible pools (0.0489 and 0.0637), as odronextamab weights one price across two. ARPI-naive first line: enzalutamide alone gave a median rPFS of 20.0 months in PREVAIL (Beer et al., Eur Urol 2017;71:151-4, doi:10.1016/j.eururo.2016.07.032), so 1 - 0.5^(12/20.0) = 34.02%. Restated without working capital build: over 2023 to 2025 PFE's cash flow statement shows receivables up $25mm, inventories up $1,462mm, payables down $1,792mm, a working capital build of $3,279mm, 1.77% of revenue. new_note: The constant hazard fits the trial: it predicts 43.7% still on drug at week 96 against 46.3% observed completing 25 cycles. The plain form 1 - 0.5^(52/80.3) = 0.362 would carry patients past the protocol's 25-cycle cap
new_source: CREST (Nat Med 2025;31(8):2806-2814, PMC12353837, opened): 'The median duration of sasanlimab treatment was 80.3 weeks (range, 4.0-103.9) in Arm A', 46.3% completed all 25 cycles, adverse events the most frequent reason for stopping (31.8%). At a constant hazard 0.5^(52/80.3) = 63.8% remain after a year and none after two, since the course ends at 25 cycles, so the stock turns over as though 1 / (1 + 0.638) = 61.0% stopped each year, the form the MRK R-DXD seed uses for a two-year capped course

new_note: Judgement. The 2021 and 2022 COVID years are excluded because a 36% margin on a vaccine windfall is not what this company earns. Restated before interest: PFE paid $8,181mm of interest inside operating cash flow over 2023 to 2025, 4.40% of revenue. The free cash flow above is struck after it and the valuation already charges the debt by subtracting net debt, so the charge falls by that much, from 22.18% to 17.77%. Checked at replacement capex: no plant depreciation on file for every year, and no amortisation line to take it out of the combined figure, so the charge stands. Restated without one-off cash: PFE's free cash flow over 2023 to 2025 carried $1,350mm of deal payments in operating cash flow, capital allocation whose assets the book values separately; $63mm of legal settlements; $4,400mm of US transition tax (2023 instalment 1,000mm; 2024 instalment 1,300mm; 2025 instalment 2,100mm). None recurs, so the charge falls from 17.77% to 14.52%. Restated without working capital build: over 2023 to 2025 PFE's cash flow statement shows receivables up $25mm, inventories up $1,462mm, payables down $1,792mm, a working capital build of $3,279mm, 1.77% of revenue. Growth ties that cash up once, not on every product for ever, so the charge falls from 14.52% to 12.66%.

new_note: 2% of the unvaccinated pool a year, a third of the RSV vaccines' first-season pace and level with CD388. Against it: four doses rather than one, a missed primary statistical criterion that may narrow any recommendation, a pool that counts everyone in a risk area, 68% of US providers willing to recommend in 2022, down from 73% in 2018 (Bostic TD et al., Vaccine 2025, doi 10.1016/j.vaccine.2025.127495), and LYMErix, withdrawn three years after its 1998 approval amid declining sales (Nigrovic LE, Thompson KM, Epidemiol Infect 2007;135(1):1-8). For it: nothing is displaced, as no Lyme vaccine is sold, and a vaccine ACIP recommends carries no cost sharing for most insured patients. The build peaks at $1,461mm in 2032 with ex-US, about 1.57 million US courses a year, and by 2046 has vaccinated about 31% of the US pool, under half the 64% who say they are willing. Valneva's 20-F (0001628280-26-018808) estimates the global market for a Lyme vaccine to exceed $1 billion, which this sits above; at 1.5% the peak is $1,111mm

new_note: a comparator, not relutrigine's price, which is not published before approval. The uptake anchor converts Skyclarys revenue to patients at this same net, so the level cancels: what transfers is Skyclarys's US revenue per eligible patient, $69,022 a year
new_source: reused from vrtx_vx_670.csv: Skyclarys (omaveloxolone), a wholesale acquisition cost of $370,000 a year at its FDA approval (Drug Discovery & Development, 'Reata sets $370,000 annual cost for new nerve disorder drug', 2023-03-03), the first and only approved therapy for Friedreich ataxia (Biogen FY2025 10-K, 0000875045-26-000013). Praxis names Skyclarys, Evrysdi and Sephience as the commercial pricing analogues for relutrigine (8-K exhibit 99.2, 0001689548-26-000082, slide 6, 'Pricing for Recent Approvals Reflects Significant Value to Patients')

new_note: it cancels in the uptake anchor, which converts Skyclarys revenue to patients at the same net of $267,251. Children with a DEE are often covered by Medicaid, whose rebates run deeper than Part D's; the anchor makes the choice immaterial to revenue
new_source: reused from vrtx_vx_670.csv: Vertex's derived gross-to-net for its specialty orals, Kalydeco's CMS Part D 2024 spend per beneficiary of $273,600 against its $378,786 WAC, 72.2% of list

new_note: the analogue's own rate, used in the uptake fit so the fitted capture is consistent with it. Case for higher: anti-seizure medicines are often switched when seizures return, and DEE carries a high early mortality. Case for lower: EMBOLD's open-label extension shows seizure reduction still deepening at eleven months and 'No dose reduction of relutrigine required' (8-K exhibit 99.2, 0001689548-26-000082, slide 18)
new_source: reused from vrtx_vx_670.csv: Gunther K et al., Neurol Ther 2025;14(3):1105-1114 (doi:10.1007/s40120-025-00749-3): of 236 people prescribed omaveloxolone at the Children's Hospital of Philadelphia, 21 (8.9%) permanently stopped in the first year

The book's route, the earliest Phase 3 primary completion plus two calendar years, gives 2027 as well (NCT05818553, primary completion 2025-11-12, actual)

new_note: stated on the filing, since the asset is outside the gate model (not big pharma). Case for higher: the study's rare disease rate is 93.6% (n=172), EMBOLD was stopped early for efficacy on the data monitoring committee's recommendation, and the BIMO inspection 'was completed successfully, and no form 483 was issued' (same 10-Q). Case for lower: the extension followed 'additional sensitivity analyses of existing clinical data', which says the FDA questioned how the primary analysis holds, and the registrational cohort is one study of 51 treated patients
new_source: published: BIO, Informa and QLS, Clinical Development Success Rates 2011-2020 (February 2021), Figure 2: NDA/BLA to approval for Neurology, 86.7% (n=165), the rate dyn_dyne_251.csv and stok_zorevunersen.csv take at the same gate. (2) A six-cycle course nets $110,435: 2025 Part B spend per claim of $19,510.12 x 6 = $117,061, divided by 1.06. One claim is one dose: in 2024, 1,616,227 mg over 10,844 claims = 149 mg, one 1.8 mg/kg dose. That gives 7,513 course-equivalents. (3) First-line share: Medicare claims were 3,924 in 2022, before the April 2023 first-line label, and 13,091 in 2025. If relapsed use held flat, first line is 70.0%, a lower bound. That gives 5,261 first-line starts. (4) Polivy is a course (d=1), so starts equal the stock. The pool is each year's eligible diagnoses, 19,046 x 0.62 = 11,809. Capture was 44.6% in 2025, Polivy's second full year, and on the fitted curve below (87.3% of peak at index 1) the peak is 51.1%. JUDGEMENT: a multiple of 0.25 gives 12.8%. For: a CD20xCD3 bispecific in place of rituximab, EU approval, and r/r FL response rates near 80%. Against: US entry around 2030 behind Pola-R-CHP, with Roche (glofitamab plus Pola-R-CHP) and AbbVie/Genmab (epcoritamab plus R-CHOP) running their own first-line CD20xCD3 Phase 3s. OLYMPIA-3 compares against R-CHOP, not Pola-R-CHP. Two US CRLs, and no US lymphoma sales force. Pool crowding: this pool (11,809) differs in size from zilovertamab vedotin's relapsed slice (3,809), so the solver does not pool them, which is right for different lines.

new_note: the 0.2 multiple is the arguable figure. new_source: early-stage share of US Parkinson's patients: 47.4% of 1,251 patients were Hoehn and Yahr stage 1 to 2, against 40.4% at 2.5 to 3 and 12.2% at 4 to 5, with a mean 1.1 products in the early group (Ciepielewska M et al., J Comp Eff Res 2025;14(11):e240186, doi:10.57264/cer-2024-0186, Adelphi Parkinson's Disease Specific Programme, US, 2021-22). new_note: the multiple is the most arguable figure here. For more: no ARIA and so no MRI safety schedule, no amyloid PET or CSF confirmation, and Parkinson's is managed by neurologists who already see these patients. Against: PADOVA missed its primary endpoint, early patients are functional on levodopa and may decline a monthly infusion, and Leqembi's own maintenance moved to four-weekly in 2025. Published peaks do not settle it: GlobalData's 'over $1.5B' US peak (Clinical Trials Arena, 22 February 2021) predates PADOVA and PARAISO; Roche's FTI consensus carries CHF 0.2bn of prasinezumab sales in 2030, a risk-adjusted pre-launch year. The anchor also leans low on scope: the Part B file counts Medicare fee-for-service patients only, against a pool of every eligible US resident, and trontinemab carries the same basis
new_source: ANCHOR, Leqembi's measured capture. CMS Part B beneficiaries (HCPCS J0174): 961 in 2023 and 7,907 in 2024 (Medicare Part B Spending by Drug, dataset 76a714ad-3a2c-43ac-b76d-9dadf8f7d890) and 14,029 in 2025 (Medicare Quarterly Part B Spending by Drug, bf6a5b3b-31ee-4abb-b1ad-2607a1e7510a, '2025 (Q1-Q4)'). Stopping 17.39% a year as above, so new starts are 961, 7,907 - 961 x 0.8261 = 7,113 and 14,029 - 7,907 x 0.8261 = 7,497. Over the 2,200,000 US residents eligible for lecanemab (Dittrich A et al., Neurology 2024, doi:10.1212/WNL.0000000000209402, PMC11175644) less those already started, capture is 0.0437%, 0.3235% and 0.3420%. MULTIPLE 2.0, A JUDGEMENT: 26 Leqembi infusions a year against 13 for prasinezumab, on the reading that Leqembi's flat new starts in 2024 and 2025 against a 2.2 million pool show a bound set by infusion and MRI capacity rather than by demand. 2.0 x 0.3420% = 0.684%

Left out: 350mm USD of legal settlement in 2025, printed only in USD, rather than converted. Restated without working capital build: over 2023 to 2025 SNY's cash flow statement shows receivables up 1,702mm EUR, inventories up 1,382mm EUR, payables up 1,445mm EUR, a working capital build of 1,639mm EUR, 1.34% of revenue. Growth ties that cash up once, not on every product for ever, so the charge falls from 9.12% to 7.53%. Struck on total revenue: Sanofi's filed cost lines sit against net sales of EUR 43,626mm and other revenues of EUR 3,090mm together (FY2025 20-F 0001628280-26-008403, Note D.34.2), so each ratio is scaled by 43,626 over 46,716 and charged on every revenue the model carries. new_source: derived: SNY turned 16.69% of revenue into free cash over 2023 to 2025 against the 25.5% its filed expense lines leave. Restated before interest: SNY paid 1,631mm EUR of interest inside operating cash flow over 2023 to 2025, 1.33% of revenue. The free cash flow above is struck after it and the valuation already charges the debt by subtracting net debt, so the charge falls by that much, from 10.45% to 9.12%. Checked at replacement capex: no plant depreciation on file for every year, and no amortisation line to take it out of the combined figure, so the charge stands. Checked without one-off cash: deal payments are booked under investing, so free cash flow never carried them, and no settlement or transition tax is stated for the window, so the charge stands. Left out: 350mm USD of legal settlement in 2025, printed only in USD, rather than converted. Restated without working capital build: over 2023 to 2025 SNY's cash flow statement shows receivables up 1,702mm EUR, inventories up 1,382mm EUR, payables up 1,445mm EUR, a working capital build of 1,639mm EUR, 1.34% of revenue. Growth ties that cash up once, not on every product for ever, so the charge falls from 9.12% to 7.53%. Struck on total revenue: Sanofi's filed cost lines sit against net sales of EUR 43,626mm and other revenues of EUR 3,090mm together (FY2025 20-F 0001628280-26-008403, Note D.34.2), so each ratio is scaled by 43,626 over 46,716 and charged on every revenue the model carries. The book's costs are the filed ones either way; this shares them across the revenue that earned them. Rebuilt on the book's own ratios on 0.3485 of the revenue they are struck on, against 0.2098 the filings leave as cash over 2023 to 2025 (free cash flow before interest, at replacement capex, without one-off cash and without working capital build), so the charge is 13.8760%.

Measured anchor: upadacitinib held 12.1% of US UC patients on advanced therapy in its fourth calendar year (Singh S et al., J Crohn's Colitis 2025, as mrk_tulisokibart.csv carries it). Reproduced on the pool (170,408 = 1,253,000 x 0.136; incidence 2,840), the curve (k 1.005, midpoint 2.15) and 27.5% discontinuation, the anchor peak is 0.1009. Identity on that path: year 0 stock 1,806 = 1,806 starts over 173,248 (1.04%). Year 1: 5,520 less 1,310 carried = 4,211 over 174,281 (2.42%). Year 2: 12,070 less 4,002 = 8,067 over 172,910 (4.67%). Year 3: 20,619 less 8,751 = 11,869 over 167,683 (7.08%), and the stock is 12.1% of the pool. Multiple 0.25, a judgement, half of the 0.5 tulisokibart takes. For: the highest Phase 2b UC effect reported for a TL1A (placebo-adjusted remission 27.4% at the high dose) and subcutaneous induction where tulisokibart and afimkibart load intravenously. Against: it is the third TL1A to market, behind tulisokibart (2028) and afimkibart (UC Phase 3 completes 2027-01-30), launching in 2030 into a UC market with the IL-23s, JAKs, S1Ps and vedolizumab, and Sanofi has no IBD franchise. Crowding: pool_crowding.solve with tulisokibart gives no rationed year. Duvakitug keeps 0.862 of its uncrowded peak, and tulisokibart falls from 1.0 to 0.931. Afimkibart will ration all three once it is modelled. Re-solved 2026-10-05 after untreated patients were given an exit (carryover P/(P+I)): the same target now needs 0.0262763, was 0.0252 (the anchor path, now at carryover 0.9836, solves to 0.105105, was 0.100904, times the multiple of 0.25).

new_note: the 0.25 is the most arguable figure here. For more: it would be the first labelled advanced therapy in MC with nothing else approved beyond budesonide. CROSS-CHECK: at population level 13 of 450 Olmsted patients (2.9%) were moved to any other therapy after budesonide, and a Belgian tertiary centre started advanced therapy in 12.6% of 239 MC patients (Taelman T et al., Acta Gastroenterol Belg 2026, PMID 42417633)

new_note: lifelong daily oral therapy for a genetic lysosomal disease
new_source: LEAP2MONO design, per Sanofi's press release of 2026-05-28 (https://www.sanofi.com/en/media-room/press-releases/2026/2026-05-28-05-00-00-3302498): once-daily oral venglustat against intravenous ERT every two weeks

new_note: Judgement on the comparator: Cerezyme is the ERT that GD3 patients take today and the active comparator in LEAP2MONO, so it matches on disease, setting and the patients venglustat would move. Part B carries 138 of Cerezyme's 178 Medicare beneficiaries in 2025, and the Part D row ($359,278.37 over 40, Medicare Quarterly Part D Spending by Drug 4ff7c618-4e40-483a-b390-c8a58c94fa15) is not summed in because it is gross of rebates where Part B is paid on ASP, so the two take different discounts. Case against: venglustat is an oral GCS inhibitor like Cerdelga, $316,673.10 per Part D beneficiary in 2025 (168), and would be dispensed under Part D; VPRIV sits at $301,793.29 per Part B beneficiary (107). No list price for venglustat exists before approval.
new_source: Cerezyme (imiglucerase, HCPCS J1786), CMS Medicare Part B Quarterly Spending by Drug (data.cms.gov dataset bf6a5b3b-31ee-4abb-b1ad-2607a1e7510a), row '2025 (Q1-Q4)': $44,631,955.83 over 138 beneficiaries = $323,419.97 a beneficiary, not annualised. In EUR because the engine models Sanofi in its reporting currency: $323,419.97 at EUR/USD 1.1367 (ECB via fetchers/fx_ecb.py, 2026-09-24, fx_rates) is EUR 284,525.35

new_note: follows the anchor's basis: the price above is Cerezyme's Part B figure, so net is 94.3% of it. Case against: venglustat would be dispensed under Part D, where rebates come off its own list price
new_source: Social Security Act section 1847A: Medicare Part B pays 106% of average sales price, and ASP is already net of manufacturer discounts and rebates, so the manufacturer's price is the CMS figure divided by 1.06, 5.66% below it (backend/gross_to_net.py: the halving convention is measured on Part D and does not apply to Part B)

new_note: Judgement on the analogue: eliglustat is the only marketed oral GCS inhibitor, the class venglustat is in. Case against: trial persistence overstates real-world persistence; in a single-centre Israeli cohort switched from ERT to eliglustat, 12 of 29 stopped at a median of 4 months, 11 for adverse events (J Clin Med 2022;11:6265, PMC9659144). On the other side, 15 of the 74 trial withdrawals were for pregnancy, which the protocols required
new_source: Peterschmitt MJ et al., Orphanet J Rare Dis 2019;14:128 (doi:10.1186/s13023-019-1085-6, PMC6555985), Table 1: 74 active withdrawals among 393 patients over 1,400 patient-years of eliglustat in the four completed trials. A constant hazard of 74/1,400 = 0.0529 a patient-year gives 1 - exp(-0.0529) = 5.15% a year
new_unit: share of treated stock stopping per year

new_note: approval at the end of November 2026 makes 2027 the first full year on sale
new_source: Sanofi press release 2026-05-28: FDA priority review with a target action date of 2026-11-25. LEAP2MONO (NCT05222906) primary completion 2025-10-02, plus two years, gives the same year

new_note: wholly owned, Genzyme origin; no partner or royalty named in any source found
new_source: Sanofi FY2025 20-F (0001628280-26-008403), pipeline table: 'venglustat Oral GCS inhibitor' in Fabry disease and Gaucher disease type 3 carries no collaboration footnote, where partnered rows such as 'frexalimab (c)' carry one. ClinicalTrials.gov lists Sanofi as sole lead sponsor of LEAP2MONO (NCT05222906)

new_note: Gaucher is not in data/epidemiology.csv and no other seed carries it, so the count is cited here. Restricted to type 3 because the filing is for GD3. Case against, lower: GOS itself counted 26 GD3 among the 969 patients with a subtype recorded (2.7%), which gives 162; Orphadata (en_product9_prev.xml, ORPHA:77261) puts GD3 point prevalence in Europe at 0.05 per 100,000, 166 on the 2020 US Census count of 331,449,281. Upper bound: Sanofi's US HCP page (pro.campus.sanofi/us/gaucher-disease/articles/recognize-and-manage-gaucher-disease-type-3) says fewer than 10% of US Gaucher patients have neurological symptoms (types 2 and 3), at most 600 of 6,000
new_source: Pfizer, Gaucher disease overview (https://www.pfizer.com/disease-and-conditions/gaucher-disease): 'As of 2018 approximately 6,000 people in the United States were diagnosed with Gaucher disease'. new_note: n=5, from 1992 to 2018, before the 2022 FDORA procedures that make withdrawal quicker. The case for more: the closest analogue, Nippon Shinyaku's exon 53 PMO Viltepso, missed its confirmatory RACER53 in 2024 and is still marketed (openFDA drugsfda NDA212154, marketing status Prescription, read 2026-10-12); the FDA accepted both sNDAs for review; and the analysis leaving out COVID-affected participants reads P=0.09 (8-K 0001193125-25-262591, Exhibit 99.1). The case for less: the primary endpoint missed at P=0.309 in a placebo-controlled study of 225, and the FDA asked Sarepta to stop ELEVIDYS shipments in July 2025 and narrowed its label in November 2025 (10-Q 0001193125-26-335003, Note 1)
new_source: published analogue: Omae K, Onishi A, Sahker E, Furukawa TA, US Food and Drug Administration accelerated approval program for nononcology drug indications between 1992 and 2018, JAMA Netw Open 2022;5(9):e2230973, doi:10.1001/jamanetworkopen.2022.30973, Table 4. Of the eight nononcology indications whose confirmatory trial failed to verify clinical efficacy, five had no other trial that verified it: hydroxyprogesterone caproate (Makena, withdrawn by the FDA on 2023-04-06, after the paper's follow-up), dalfopristin/quinupristin (withdrawn), rifapentine (converted, on equivalence), mafenide acetate and midodrine (still under accelerated approval). Three of five stayed on the market, 0.60. pos = 0.60 + 0.40 x pos_failure = 0.6 + 0.40 x 0.2964: the product stays on the market (converted, or left under accelerated approval) or is withdrawn after the decision of 2027-02-28

new_note: A refusal that leaves the accelerated approval in place is worth the same, which is why pos counts staying on the market rather than conversion
new_source: convention, the converted case is the marketed forecast: the FDA converts the accelerated approval to traditional approval at the PDUFA target action date of 2027-02-28 (Sarepta's release of 2026-06-30 as RTTNews and BioPharm International report it: 'The FDA has set a Prescription Drug User Fee Act (PDUFA) target action date of February 28, 2027'; sNDAs submitted in April 2026 and accepted in June 2026, 10-Q 0001193125-26-335003), on ESSENCE (NCT02500381) and real-world evidence: the label stands and the product sells as modelled

new_note: a floor in timing: withdrawal is its own proceeding. CDER proposed withdrawing Makena in 2020 after its confirmatory trial failed in 2019, and the approval ended on 2023-04-06 (FDA press release of that day), so a slower withdrawal keeps more. Rest-of-world early access sales may outlast a US withdrawal; none is kept
new_source: judgement on timing, reasoned from the label: the accelerated approval is withdrawn at the decision of 2027-02-28 and the product stops selling, US and rest of world. new_note: acquired IPR&D charges above all, then amortisation, restructuring and capital spending. Casgevy is left at zero: it reproduces the CASGEVY workbook line for line and is what this engine was validated against, so its cost basis stays the workbook's
new_source: derived: Vertex generated $12,074mm of free cash flow on $49,396mm of revenue over the five years to 2025, a 24.44% margin, against the 33.0% its cost of sales, SG&A and R&D leave. Five years rather than three because operating cash flow was negative $493mm in 2024 on the Alpine acquisition, which takes a three-year window to 17.5% and lets one deal set the rate. Solved so the modelled book reproduces the margin rather than taken off a single line. Restated before interest: VRTX paid $195mm of interest inside operating cash flow over 2021 to 2025, 0.39% of revenue. The free cash flow above is struck after it and the valuation already charges the debt by subtracting net debt, so the charge falls by that much, from 10.33% to 9.94%. Restated at replacement capex: VRTX spent $1,375mm on plant over 2021 to 2025 against $758mm of plant depreciation, 1.25% of revenue above what keeps the plant running. Taken at depreciation, the charge falls from 9.94% to 8.47%. Restated without one-off cash: VRTX's free cash flow over 2021 to 2025 carried $6,517mm of deal payments in operating cash flow, capital allocation whose assets the book values separately. None recurs, so the charge falls from 8.47% to 0.00%. Restated to the amortisation floor: the filed cost lines leave a 39.05% pre-tax margin where the cash over 2021 to 2025 supports 43.77%, so the charge rebuilds at -4.72%. It was held at nil, but VRTX books $20mm of non-cash amortisation of acquired intangibles inside cost of sales in FY2025 (0000875320-26-000056), 0.17% of revenue, so the charge stops at that floor: -0.17%. Restated without working capital build: over 2021 to 2025 VRTX's cash flow statement shows receivables up $1,164mm, inventories up $1,594mm, payables up $288mm, a working capital build of $2,470mm, 5.00% of revenue. Growth ties that cash up once, not on every product for ever, so the charge was held at the amortisation floor, -0.17% where the filed figures rebuild it at -4.72%, and stays there.

new_source: derived and found to be nil: AbbVie generated $17,816mm of free cash flow on $61,160mm of revenue in FY2025, a 29.13% margin, against the 28.95% its cost of sales, SG&A and R&D leave. Checked without one-off cash: deal payments are booked under investing, so free cash flow never carried them, and no settlement or transition tax is stated for the window, so the charge stands. Restated to the amortisation floor: the filed cost lines leave a 32.46% pre-tax margin where the cash over 2025 supports 38.40%, so the charge rebuilds at -5.94%. new_note: AbbVie books its amortisation of acquired intangibles inside cost of sales, $7,377mm of it, which is why its 29.8% cost of sales is so far above Pfizer's 25.7% and why the same test that charged Pfizer 22% charges AbbVie nothing. The older windows would imply a credit, not a cost: 33.6% over three years and 36.3% over five, both above the model, because they carry peak Humira. A backward window cannot be used to charge a company whose margin is falling
new_source: derived and found to be nil: AbbVie generated $17,816mm of free cash flow on $61,160mm of revenue in FY2025, a 29.13% margin, against the 28.95% its cost of sales, SG&A and R&D leave. The two reconcile to within a fifth of a point, which is why this is zero rather than absent: the check was run and it found nothing to charge. Restated before interest: ABBV paid $3,002mm of interest inside operating cash flow over 2025, 4.91% of revenue. The free cash flow above is struck after it and the valuation already charges the debt by subtracting net debt, so adding it back only widens a gap the filed lines already leave, and the charge stays nil. Restated at replacement capex: ABBV spent $1,214mm on plant over 2025 against $762mm of plant depreciation, 0.74% of revenue above what keeps the plant running. Taken at depreciation, the charge stays nil. Checked without one-off cash: deal payments are booked under investing, so free cash flow never carried them, and no settlement or transition tax is stated for the window, so the charge stands. Restated to the amortisation floor: the filed cost lines leave a 32.46% pre-tax margin where the cash over 2025 supports 38.40%, so the charge rebuilds at -5.94%. It was held at nil, but ABBV books $7,377mm of non-cash amortisation of acquired intangibles inside cost of sales in FY2025 (0001551152-26-000008), 12.06% of revenue, so the charge takes the rebuilt figure: -5.94%. Restated without working capital build: over 2025 ABBV's cash flow statement shows receivables up $1,490mm, inventories up $234mm, payables and accrued liabilities up $951mm, a working capital build of $773mm, 1.26% of revenue. Growth ties that cash up once, not on every product for ever, so the charge falls from -5.94% to -7.35%.

new_source: Opdivo (nivolumab, HCPCS J9299), CMS Part B 2025 from the quarterly companion bf6a5b3b-31ee-4abb-b1ad-2607a1e7510a, row '2025 (Q1-Q4)': $1,996,916,016.40 over 26,991 beneficiaries = $73,984.51 per beneficiary. Discount: the biosimilar-to-reference ASP ratio in the first full year after Amgen launched Mvasi and Kanjinti in July 2019, from CMS Part B spending per dosage unit in 2020 (drug_demand): Mvasi $62.43 against Avastin $70.86, and Kanjinti $81.55 against Herceptin $91.78. ASP ratios are 0.8739 (Mvasi) and 0.8818 (Kanjinti), mean 0.8778. $73,984.51 x 0.8778 = $64,947

new_note: Judgement on which comparator. The engine reads this key (forecast._price_factor), and a biosimilar's defining economics is its price erosion after launch: Mvasi's ASP fell to 30% of Avastin's by 2024 and Kanjinti's to 17% of Herceptin's. Leaving it null would hold the launch price flat for the whole horizon, the most aggressive reading. Mvasi's rate is taken rather than the 29.9% mean of the two, because the engine compounds one constant rate across the horizon and declines slow after year four. Mvasi also held its Medicare volume (12,306 beneficiaries in 2020, 13,212 in 2024), where Kanjinti's fell from 7,550 to 3,365 against four other trastuzumab biosimilars (Horn et al.). The case for faster: Kanjinti's 36.7%, and a crowded first wave of PD-1 biosimilars. The case for slower: Kim et al. (JCO Oncol Pract 2026, doi:10.1200/OP-26-00259) put the bevacizumab biosimilar mean allowed amount at $69.70 (2019) and $33.36 (2023), 16.8% a year on the allowed basis, and Mvasi's own yearly ASP falls were 19.4%, 35.7%, 22.9% and 12.5%, slowing by 2024. The engine freezes the factor at the LOE year it assumes for an unlaunched biologic (launch plus 12, so 2041), where 23.1% compounded prices 2041 at 4.3% of 2029
new_source: drug_demand, CMS Part B spending per dosage unit, converted to ASP as in list_price_per_patient. The biosimilar add-on is 6% of reference ASP to September 2022 and 8% from October 2022 for a qualifying biosimilar (Inflation Reduction Act s.11403; CMS biosimilar FAQs, cms.gov/files/document/biosimilar-faqs.pdf); 2022 is taken at 6.5%. Mvasi ASP $58.42 (2020), $47.11, $30.30, $23.37, $20.45 (2024): 1 - (20.45/58.42)^(1/4) = 23.1% a year. Kanjinti $76.35 (2020) to $12.24 (2024): 36.7% a year
new_unit: annual share of net price lost, nominal as measured

new_note: Judgement on method. The pool is Opdivo's own patients across every indication, so this is measured on them rather than taken from one melanoma trial's median. Under a constant hazard in a steady state, the share of a year's treated patients (beneficiaries) still on drug into the next year equals the patient-years per beneficiary, 0.374, so the engine's stock (S = S x (1-d) + new) is the count of beneficiaries the per-beneficiary price is quoted on. The implied hazard is 1.67 a year, a median time on drug of 5.0 months. eligible_pct is built from this value (new starts = treated patients x 0.6256), so changing one without the other moves the steady-state patient count. The case against: dose holds, weight-based doses and the 1 mg/kg nivolumab induction with ipilimumab lower mg per patient-year and overstate stopping; fixed one-year adjuvant use understates it
new_source: drug_demand Opdivo, CMS Part B 2024, the latest year that carries dosage units (the 2025 quarterly file has none): 62,964,187 dosage units over 26,951 beneficiaries = 2,336 mg per beneficiary. HCPCS J9299 is 'injection, nivolumab, 1 mg'. A full labelled year is 6,240 mg (240 mg x 26 or 480 mg x 13; Opdivo USPI), so a beneficiary averages 0.3744 of a year on drug, and 1 - 0.3744 = 0.6256. The ratio is stable across 2020 to 2024 (0.392, 0.382, 0.382, 0.378, 0.374)

new_note: The pool is Opdivo's own IV-treated patients, not a disease. A biosimilar takes the reference product's patients across every labelled indication it is extrapolated to (lung, kidney, bladder, gastro-oesophageal, liver, melanoma and others), not the melanoma population its similarity trials enrolled. Melanoma is used only because the indication must be one of the asset's own. The share is a scaling of the book's melanoma incidence to Opdivo's IV new starts, not a melanoma eligibility filter. Check: 77,396 x $69,797 = $5,402mm, the IV share of FY2025 US nivolumab revenue, so the pool reproduces the reference's revenue at its own net price. At 39% penetration the steady-state treated stock is 0.39 x 77,396 = 30,184 US patients, before the ex-US multiple. The case for higher: BMS's net revenue per patient sits below ASP because of Medicaid rebates and 340B, so the count understates patients. The case for lower: Qvantig reached 12.7% of US nivolumab revenue in Q2 2026 ($206mm against $1,417mm) and BMS will convert more before 2028. new_note: Judgement: a multiple of 1.0 on Amgen's own measured first-mover share of the molecule in Medicare, from two products that agree at 39%. This is ABP 206's share, not the whole biosimilar class, which reached 61.3% of bevacizumab in Medicare Part B by 2023 (Kim et al.). It assumes ABP 206 is in the first wave, which Amgen states (Fierce Pharma, 2026-09-16). The case for lower: a first mover's share erodes as later entrants undercut. Kanjinti's Medicare beneficiaries fell from 7,550 (2021) to 3,365 (2024), and Mvasi held at most 51% of biosimilar beneficiaries by 2023 (12,502 against Zirabev's 12,056, drug_demand) as further entrants arrived. The engine holds this share flat. Patent carve-outs, BMS contracting and the move to Qvantig all push the same way. The case for higher: commercial payers can mandate biosimilars
new_source: Kanjinti, Amgen's first-to-market trastuzumab biosimilar, held 39.6% of Medicare trastuzumab claims by December 2020, against Herceptin's 45.3% (Chen et al., 'Cancer Drug Trastuzumab And Its Biosimilars Compete On Price For Market Share', Health Aff 2023;42(6):779-784, doi:10.1377/hlthaff.2022.01448, Medicare fee-for-service claims 2019 to 2020, as reported by AJMC, 'Trastuzumab Biosimilars Successfully Drove Down Prices', 2023-06-05). Cross-check on Mvasi: bevacizumab biosimilars held 57.5% of Medicare Part B in 2021 (Kim et al., JCO Oncol Pract 2026, doi:10.1200/OP-26-00259, PMID 42413074). Mvasi had 15,239 of the 22,574 Part B beneficiaries on the only two bevacizumab biosimilars then marketed (Zirabev 7,335; drug_demand), 67.5%, and 0.575 x 0.675 = 38.8%

new_note: Judgement: a measured class curve for an IV oncology biosimilar in Medicare, used because the book has no modelled biosimilar. The branded-launch curves it carries (Enhertu, k 1.08) are too slow for buy-and-bill substitution. Amgen's own products peaked as fast or faster: Medicare beneficiaries went from 12,306 to 15,239 for Mvasi and 6,950 to 7,550 for Kanjinti between the first and second full years (drug_demand). The engine applies the curve to new starts only, while the observed share included switching patients already on the reference, so the modelled stock lags the observed ramp in years one and two, which understates early revenue. The case for slower: Horn et al. (doi:10.1200/OP.22.00639) show trastuzumab biosimilars at 7% of the market in their first year and 32% in their second, and litigation could stage entry

new_source: Same fit: midpoint = -logit(0.520) / k = -0.082 / 2.64 = -0.03, so half of peak is reached in the first full year (2029), as the bevacizumab biosimilars did in 2020

Under a constant hazard in a steady state, the share of a year's treated patients still on drug into the next year equals the patient-years per beneficiary, 0.411, so the engine's stock is the count of beneficiaries the per-beneficiary price is quoted on. The implied hazard is 0.89 a year, a median time on drug of 9.4 months. eligible_pct is built from this value (new starts = treated patients x 0.5886), so changing one without the other moves the steady-state patient count. The case against: dose holds and the 2 mg/kg paediatric dose lower mg per patient-year and overstate stopping; the 24-month and one-year caps in the label mean a patient who stays well still stops, which a constant hazard spreads evenly

The value written before, 0.0063, was solved on a logistic fitted to Kerendia's beneficiary stock and then used as the penetration ramp, which reads a stock as penetration. new_note: the progression, death and unfitness that keep patients from consolidation are left in the pool and carried by the penetration anchor below, which is measured on the same concurrent chemoradiation starters. SEER's window is 2000 to 2013, before durvalumab; over it the stage IIIA share of the cohort rose from 33.2% to 46.5% (Hansen RN et al.), so the mix is still moving
new_source: Two shares multiplied. (1) Unresectable stage III NSCLC given chemotherapy and radiation as first treatment is 5.369% of all lung cancer diagnoses: of 239,602 lung cancers in SEER over 2000 to 2013, 33,507 were unresectable stage III NSCLC and 12,865 received chemotherapy and radiation (Hansen RN et al., BMC Cancer 2020;20:276, PMC7132866). Over the NSCLC pool that is 5.369% / 0.85 = 6.317%. (2) Concurrent rather than sequential: 35,534 of 42,220 patients given chemoradiation for non-surgically treated stage III NSCLC in the National Cancer Database received it concurrently, 84.2% (Miller ED et al., Radiat Oncol 2018;13:196, PMC6173899: 13,940 of 16,668 elderly and 21,594 of 25,552 younger). PACIFIC-9 enrols patients who have not progressed after concurrent platinum chemoradiation. 0.06317 x 0.8416 = 0.0532, about 10,250 patients a year

new_note: the 0.5 multiple is the most arguable figure here. Durvalumab's own uptake in this setting was immediate: 60.4% of potentially eligible Flatiron patients in the first three months after approval, 66.5% over 18 months (Jairam V et al., J Clin Oncol 2021;39(15_suppl):e20550)
new_source: ANCHOR, measured: 262 of 426 US patients with unresectable stage III NSCLC who started concurrent chemoradiation, 61.5%, went on to consolidation durvalumab (Arunachalam A et al., PLoS One 2024;19(11):e0314156, PMC11588217, US Oncology Network, starts 2017 to 2019); death (28.3%) and progression (22.2%) were the main reasons the rest did not. That is Imfinzi's own capture of this pool, the slot oleclumab would share. MULTIPLE 0.5, A JUDGEMENT: 0.5 x 61.5% = 30.75% of each year's patients at peak. For: AstraZeneca owns the backbone and would move its own consolidation patients; in COAST the combination's PFS hazard ratio against durvalumab alone was 0.44 (Barlesi F et al., Future Oncol 2024, doi:10.1080/14796694.2024.2354160); and a rival add-on trial in this setting, PACIFIC-8 with domvanalimab, was discontinued for strategic portfolio prioritisation (appendix of 27 July 2026). Against: the monalizumab arm of the same trial could take the slot instead; a blinded Phase 3 effect is usually smaller than an open-label Phase 2 one; the combination adds infusions in the first two cycles; and Tagrisso's US label now covers EGFR-mutant unresectable stage III disease after chemoradiation (DailyMed, in the book's labels table), which takes those patients out of durvalumab consolidation after the 2017 to 2019 measurement

new_note: the HRRm cohort only: AMPLITUDE, the one PARP add-on Phase 3 in this setting to report, was run in HRR-altered men, and EvoPAR-Prostate01's non-HRRm cohort would take the pool to all 40,200 if it reads out positive. Cross-check on the same basis: 79.3% of first-line mCRPC patients came from mHSPC (Hooper 2026), so 0.115 x 0.793 = 9.11% of diagnoses reach mCRPC from mHSPC, 71% of the 12.81% entering it, which leaves room for deaths before castration resistance. Devasia back-calculates from 2000 to 2017 SEER data and distant-stage incidence rose 5.3% a year in men 45 to 74 and 6.5% in men 75 and over to 2018 (Desai et al., JAMA Netw Open 2022, jamanetwork.com/journals/jamanetworkopen/fullarticle/2790041), so the pool leans low. The case for a smaller pool: AMPLITUDE enrolled every protocol-defined HRR alteration, 56% of them BRCA1 or BRCA2, yet FDA approved Akeega only 'for the treatment of patients with BRCA2-mutated metastatic castration-sensitive prostate cancer' (Johnson & Johnson press release, 2025-12-12), so a saruparib label narrower than the HRRm cohort is a live risk
new_source: Two shares multiplied. First, 12.81% of diagnoses enter metastatic castration-sensitive disease each year. 6.8% of US cases are metastatic at diagnosis and de novo cases are 45% of the men living with metastatic prostate cancer (Devasia et al., Cancer Epidemiol Biomarkers Prev 2023;32(5):659-65, doi:10.1158/1055-9965.EPI-22-1038, PMC10159917; its base case gives de novo and recurrent disease the same survival, so the incidence split is the prevalence split): 0.068 / 0.45 = 15.11% of diagnoses become metastatic. Less the men whose first metastases are already castration-resistant: 1,019 of 5,096 US patients starting first-line mCRPC therapy (20.0%) came from non-metastatic CRPC (Flatiron; Hooper et al., JAMA Netw Open 2026;9(6):e2620750, doi:10.1001/jamanetworkopen.2026.20750), on the book's 11.5% mCRPC share: 0.1511 - 0.115 x 0.200 = 12.81%, about 40,200 men a year. Second, 17.86% carry a protocol-defined HRR alteration: 1,054 of 5,903 men with mCSPC prescreened for AMPLITUDE with a valid result (Attard et al., Nat Med 2025, doi:10.1038/s41591-025-03961-8). 0.1281 x 0.1786 = 0.02288, about 7,180 men a year

new_note: analogue, the most arguable figure here. The ratio does not depend on the Spanish positivity rate: Adelphi's own pooled figures, HRR alterations known in 13% of mCSPC and 18% of mCRPC patients, give (0.13 / 0.1786) x (0.07 / 0.18) = 0.283, and its 38% positivity among the men tested says testing is selective, which a ratio of the two settings absorbs. The case for more: HRR gene testing in metastatic prostate cancer rose 17 points, 26% to 43%, between the 2020 and 2022-2023 waves of the same programme and AMPLITUDE supports testing as routine in mCSPC; saruparib is PARP1-selective, where 25% of AMPLITUDE's niraparib arm needed a transfusion. The case for less: this gives saruparib the whole PARP class, and FDA approved Akeega (niraparib with abiraterone) in BRCA2-mutated mCSPC on 2025-12-12 (Johnson & Johnson press release), so saruparib would launch as the second PARP option in the setting; Akeega reached 93 Medicare Part D beneficiaries in 2025 (CMS file 4ff7c618); and in first-line mCRPC, where the PARP and ARPI combinations are labelled, PARP-based regimens stayed under 2.5% of starts across 2021 to 2025 (Hooper 2026)
new_source: Decomposed into who is found and who is treated once found, on US rates because the model and the treatment share are US. new_source: derived: solved so the segment's pre-tax cash before interest is what Bayer reports. Bayer Annual Report 2025, note [4] table B 4/2 'Key data by segment': Pharmaceuticals, and the segment key data tables in Bayer Annual Report 2025 (A 2.2.2/1, /4 and /7): EBITDA before special items of EUR 4,525mm, less restructuring of 248mm (a recurring cost, so kept in), less cash flow-relevant capital expenditures of 870mm, is 3,407mm. Bayer's unallocated costs are then shared by sales: All Other Segments' EBITDA before special items of 277mm, Enabling Functions and Consolidation's -662mm, 45mm of restructuring in the Reconciliation and the 426mm of group capital expenditure the three segments do not report, -856mm in all, of which 39.40% (-337mm) is this segment's share of the 45,253mm the three segments sell. Without one-off cash: litigation special items (group EUR 7,455mm in 2025) are left out and the provisions they built are carried as claims on equity instead; divestment gains are left out. Restated without working capital build: EBITDA is struck before working capital, so the build is charged on growth by the book instead. Across the three segments the targets sum to 6,587mm, which is the group's EBITDA before special items of 9,669mm less 595mm of restructuring and 2,487mm of capital expenditures

The incumbent is CAR T itself, in its only measured setting: referral from community physicians to certified centres, apheresis and lymphodepletion, the same barriers a rheumatology patient meets. No US count of autologous transplants for SSc (the one-time cellular incumbent in this disease) was found. At the third-line 35.7%, p would be 0.0328. Case for lower: the 25% is shared by several CAR Ts, and zola-cel will meet rese-cel (Cabaletta), rapcabtagene autoleucel (Novartis) and bispecific T-cell engagers in SSc. Refractory SSc-ILD is not fatal within months as relapsed LBCL is, and it has chronic alternatives (tocilizumab, rituximab, nintedanib). The LBCL denominator is fit patients only, while this pool is not filtered for fitness. The class-wide autoimmune CAR T pause of September 2026 (IEC-HS after three deaths on Novartis's product) may make referrers cautious. Case for higher: patients are younger, a drug-free remission after one infusion appeals, a refractory patient faces repeated escalation decisions over years, and FDA's removal of the CAR T REMS eases logistics. This is an UPPER BOUND. It includes deaths never treated in the line, and both trials exclude primary platinum-refractory disease and require ECOG 0-1. The published alternative, Kumar et al. (ISPOR 2024, doi:10.1016/j.jval.2024.03.1253, poster), counts 917 + 1,895 + 1,715 = 4,527 PROC regimens in lines 2 to 4+ on 23,820 incident cases, a share of 0.1901. new_source: This reproduces the identity in backend/capture_anchor.py on Elahere. US revenue comes from AbbVie filings: - FY2025: $607mm (10-K 0001551152-26-000008). - FY2024: $477mm, counted only from the 12 Feb 2024 ImmunoGen close (324 of 366 days), annualised to $538.8mm. - 2026: Q2 US $161mm (10-Q 0001551152-26-000026) x 4 = $644mm. Net price per patient-year = the Part B figure / 1.06: $114,344 for 2024 and $116,413 for 2025. Stock = revenue / net price: 4,712 (2024), 5,214 (2025), 5,532 (2026, at the 2025 price). Starts = this year's stock less last year's stock x (1 - 0.7724): - 2025: 5,214 - 1,073 = 4,142. - 2026: 5,532 - 1,187 = 4,345. The all-comers PROC cohort is 21,010 x 0.5926 = 12,450. Elahere's starts are 0.3327 of it in 2025 and 0.3490 in 2026. On Elahere's own label (FRalpha-high, 36% of PROC: Matulonis et al., JCO 2023, doi:10.1200/JCO.22.01900; 36.3% in the real world: Previs et al., Gynecol Oncol 2024, doi:10.1016/j.ygyno.2024.11.010), the same starts are 92.4% and 97.0% of 4,482 a year. The incumbent has filled its niche. Peak = anchor 0.3327 (2025, the last full reported year) x multiple 0.4. The multiple is a JUDGEMENT. Case for a higher multiple: the label covers all comers with no B7-H4 cut-off. Confirmed ORR was 62% (21/34 at 5.8 mg/kg) against Elahere's 42% in MIRASOL. B7-H4 is a new target, so it can follow an FRalpha ADC. Case against: the PROC launch is about 2032, behind four rivals: - Genmab's Rina-S, an FRalpha ADC (NCT06619236, primary completion 2027-02). - R-DXd from Daiichi Sankyo and Merck (REJOICE-Ovarian01, NCT06161025, 2028-02, Breakthrough). - AZD5335 (NCT07218809, 2028-11). - Sofetabart (2030). The 62% comes from 34 patients at one dose in a single-arm trial. Elahere is modelled off its own revenue, so any share taken from it is counted twice. Carryover: at 0 (the engine's documented setting for a line of cancer therapy), the penetration is a share of each year's cohort. At the book default of 1.0, this drug's own curve converges on the whole cohort: an engine run gives about $1.8bn US at year 10, against $245mm at carryover 0. Elahere sells $607mm in the US.
