new_source: Three sourced parts. (1) 5,234 of 31,019 staged cases (16.87%) were distant at diagnosis (Patel & Benipal, Cureus 2019;11(2):e4120, PMID 31037234, Table 1). (2) Estimated 15-year recurrence-free survival after surgery without adjuvant therapy was 59.9%, so 40.1% recur (Joensuu H et al., Lancet Oncol 2012;13:265-74, doi:10.1016/S1470-2045(11)70299-6, PMID 22153892, 2,560 patients pooled). 0.1687 + 0.8313 x 0.401 = 0.5021 of each year's diagnoses reach advanced disease. (3) The label reach: StrateGIST 3 (NCT07218926; ASCO 2026 TPS11588) excludes GIST that is wild-type for both KIT and PDGFRA and GIST with an activating PDGFRA exon 18 mutation. In advanced GIST (MetaGIST) KIT mutations are found in 82.8% and PDGFRA in 2.1% (Emile JF et al., Med Oncol 2012;29(3):1765-72, doi:10.1007/s12032-011-0074-y, PMID 21953054). 0.5021 x 0.828 = 0.4157

new_note: JUDGEMENT on the multiple, the formula the zigakibart seed cross-checks with. The case for higher: velzatinib is a single agent where the pioneer is a two-drug combination carrying sunitinib's toxicity, its second-line cohort showed a 13.7-month median PFS, and a PFS win could also displace imatinib dose escalation, which the 52.8% leaves out. The case for lower: StrateGIST 3 compares against sunitinib alone, not the combination that will be standard by readout, so velzatinib may launch without a head-to-head answer to it; Hsu's denominator excludes patients who received neither option, so the share overstates capture of this pool; the setting is Taiwan, not the US. Bezuclastinib is not in the book, so pool_crowding cannot see it and the cut has to sit here.
new_source: Two parts. (1) Sunitinib's measured second-line share: Hsu JT et al., Oncotarget 2017;8(41):71128-37, doi:10.18632/oncotarget.16795, PMID 29050348 (Taiwan National Health Insurance Research Database, July 2004 to December 2010): of 521 advanced GIST patients failing first-line imatinib 400 mg and treated with dose escalation or sunitinib, 125 escalated then switched to sunitinib and 150 switched directly, so 275 (52.78%) received sunitinib after imatinib. (2) An order-of-entry cut, because velzatinib will not be the first branded drug to beat sunitinib in second line: Cogent's bezuclastinib plus sunitinib beat sunitinib in the PEAK Phase 3 (median PFS 16.5 against 9.2 months, HR 0.50, Cogent 8-K 10 November 2025) and its NDA was accepted with priority review and a PDUFA date of 2026-11-30 (Cogent release, 28 May 2026), more than three years before velzatinib's 2030 start. Urban et al., Management Science 1986, put a second entrant's share at 2^-0.49 = 0.712 of the pioneer's, so the second of two takes 0.712 / 1.712 = 41.59% of the class. 0.5278 x 0.4159 = 0.2195

new_note: an upper reading: it gives this drug the place of the line's leading medicine. Enzalutamide's share has also fallen within the cohort: 101 of the 412 patients indexed 2019 to 2022 (24.5%) against 29.7% over 2013 to 2022 (same paper, Table 1, index year by therapy). The case for less: the book's opevesostat (20%) and ifinatamab deruxtecan (25%) claim the same post-ARPI pool, Pluvicto has been labelled after an ARPI and before a taxane since an efficacy supplement approved 2025-03-28 (NDA215833), and generic abiraterone leaves payers a cheap second ARPI to step through. The case for more: 59% of the 22 patients given two or more cycles had a PSA50 response (Halda, AACR-NCI-EORTC, 2025-10-24), where a second ARPI gives little. new_source: ANCHOR, a measured share of the same line. Among 804 ARPI-experienced US mCRPC patients who started a line after an ARPI (Narayan et al., Clin Genitourin Cancer 2024;22(6):102188, doi:10.1016/j.clgc.2024.102188, Flatiron 2013 to 2022), that first post-ARPI line was enzalutamide in 239 (29.7%), abiraterone in 191 (23.8%) and docetaxel in 171 (21.3%), and 459 (57.1%) took a second ARPI. That cohort is the eligible pool above, patients starting a line after an ARPI, so a share of it is a share of each year's eligible patients. HLD-0915 is an oral once-daily androgen receptor-directed medicine built to work after ARPI resistance, so the place it is designed to take is the second ARPI, and 29.7% is the most any one medicine holds of this line. 0.610 x 0.53 x 0.60 = 0.19398, a label pool of 4,153,888 of 21,414,000. First, 61.0% of adults with a past-year major depressive episode received treatment (NIMH, NSDUH 2021). This is any treatment, including counselling alone, so it overstates the share on an SSRI or SNRI; the label will require one. Second, 53% respond inadequately to the first SSRI: STAR*D level 1 citalopram response was 47% (Trivedi MH et al., Am J Psychiatry 2006;163:28-40, doi 10.1176/appi.ajp.163.1.28). Third, about 60% of MDD patients have clinically relevant insomnia symptoms despite an SSRI or SNRI. That figure is J&J's own, from its press release of 2026-05-11, not an independent study. This 19.4% of MDD is the adjunctive-with-insomnia share the audit asked for.

new_source: Auvelity's measured capture, using the identity in capture_anchor.py (untreated pool, no opening stock) on Axsome's filed Auvelity net revenue: $130.1mm in 2023, $291.4mm in 2024, $507.1mm in 2025. Net price per beneficiary is $2,730.57 (its 2025 Part D $5,461.14, halved), and the pool is its whole label, 21,414,000. Stock: 47,646, 106,718 and 185,712. Carried forward at 9% (discontinuation 0.91): 0, 4,288 and 9,605. New starts: 47,646, 102,430 and 176,108. Capture rates: 0.2225%, 0.4794% and 0.8282% (2025, over an untreated pool of 21,263,925). The 2025 rate is the anchor because it is the last full year with a single label. The Q2 2026 run-rate ($180.3mm times 4) gives 1.1732%, but Auvelity added Alzheimer's agitation in June 2026. The anchor at the alternative discontinuation of 0.70 is 0.7225%. MULTIPLE 0.75x, A JUDGEMENT: 0.8282% x 0.75 = 0.6212% of seltorexant's own untreated label pool. For a higher multiple: the label pool is narrow and every patient in it is actively changing therapy; J&J has psychiatry sales scale; residual insomnia is common, and against quetiapine XR seltorexant showed four times less somnolence and less weight gain. Against: only one of two placebo-controlled Phase 3s was positive (a 2.6-point MADRS gain); it was not significantly better than generic quetiapine XR; and it enters a crowded add-on class of Rexulti, Vraylar, generic aripiprazole and quetiapine, and J&J's own Caplyta. Caplyta took the adjunctive MDD label on 2025-11-06 with 4.9 and 4.5 points against placebo, so J&J may put Caplyta first. At 1.0x the peak is 0.8282%.

The pool is each year's cohort and the stock carries at 25.5% a year, so the steady stock is peak x pool / 0.745, and a stock of 5.4% needs a peak of 0.054 x 0.745 = 0.04023. That takes pregabalin's stopping as the market's (74.5% against about 77%, Schuster et al. 2026), so its share of starts is its share of users. For more: the first AT2R antagonist, a peripheral non-opioid mechanism aimed at the tolerability that makes 56.3% of starters stop within 3 months (Schuster et al.). Against: it would launch in 2033 into a market where 59.0% of starts are generic gabapentin, pregabalin and duloxetine are generic, and suzetrigine gets there first; and the last AT2R antagonist, EMA401, missed significance in DPN (-0.6 on the NRS against placebo, P=0.10, 137 of 400 planned patients) before preclinical liver toxicity stopped it (Rice ASC et al., Pain 2021;162(10):2578-2589, PMID 33675631)

new_source: Anchor: Elahere's 2025 US starts of 4,142 = 0.3327 of the all-comers PROC cohort of 12,450. The derivation is on GSK's ovarian row: - US revenue: $607mm (2025), $538.8mm (2024, annualised). - Net price: $116,413 per patient-year. - Stock: 5,214 (2025) against 4,712 (2024), with 77.24% stopping. - In 2026 the rate is 0.3490 (Q2 x 4). Peak = 0.3327 x multiple 0.5 = 0.1663. The multiple is a JUDGEMENT. The multiple is set above GSK's 0.4 because Sofe-M reaches PROC about two years earlier and holds Breakthrough. Carryover: at 0, this drug's US revenue at year 10 is about $311mm; at the book default of 1.0 it is about $1.8bn, because the curve then converges on the whole cohort.

new_note: the 0.5 is a judgement and the most arguable figure here. For more: if approved it would be the first PH-COPD therapy, as Tyvaso was in PH-ILD; once-daily; pulmonary-selective, and in a Phase 1 in PH-COPD it improved pulmonary haemodynamics without systemic vasodilation (INSIGNIA-PH-COPD design abstract, Am J Respir Crit Care Med 2025;212(Suppl 1) A65-11, citing Bajwa et al., Int J COPD 2024); and Merck already sells Ohtuvayre in COPD. new_source: derived: Merck generated $39,599mm of free cash flow on $189,294mm of revenue over 2023, 2024 and 2025, a 20.92% margin, against the 29.5% its cost of sales, SG&A and R&D leave. Solved so the modelled book reproduces that margin rather than assumed from one line's cost structure: the alliance rows carry no cost of sales and Animal Health carries its own, so a ratio taken off a single product does not reconcile the company. The window barely matters here, unlike Pfizer: the same aggregate is 21.9% over five years and 21.3% over every year on file. Restated before interest: MRK paid $3,700mm of interest inside operating cash flow over 2023 to 2025, 1.95% of revenue. The free cash flow above is struck after it and the valuation already charges the debt by subtracting net debt, so the charge falls by that much, from 12.10% to 10.14%. Restated at replacement capex: MRK spent $11,347mm on plant over 2023 to 2025 against $6,977mm of plant depreciation, 2.31% of revenue above what keeps the plant running. Taken at depreciation, the charge falls from 10.14% to 7.48%. Restated without one-off cash: MRK's free cash flow over 2023 to 2025 carried $8,300mm of deal payments in operating cash flow, capital allocation whose assets the book values separately; $572mm of legal settlements; $1,200mm of US transition tax (2025 instalment 1,200mm). None recurs, so the charge falls from 7.48% to 2.06%. Restated without working capital build: over 2023 to 2025 MRK's cash flow statement shows receivables up $2,482mm, inventories up $2,831mm, payables down $88mm, a working capital build of $5,401mm, 2.85% of revenue. Growth ties that cash up once, not on every product for ever, so the charge falls from 2.06% to -1.23%. Rebuilt on the book's own ratios on 0.3610 of the revenue they are struck on, against 0.3746 the filings leave as cash over 2023 to 2025 (free cash flow before interest, at replacement capex, without one-off cash and without working capital build), so the charge is -1.3576%.

Restated before interest: MRK paid $3,700mm of interest inside operating cash flow over 2023 to 2025, 1.95% of revenue. The free cash flow above is struck after it and the valuation already charges the debt by subtracting net debt, so the charge falls by that much, from 12.10% to 10.14%. Restated at replacement capex: MRK spent $11,347mm on plant over 2023 to 2025 against $6,977mm of plant depreciation, 2.31% of revenue above what keeps the plant running. Taken at depreciation, the charge falls from 10.14% to 7.48%. Restated without one-off cash: MRK's free cash flow over 2023 to 2025 carried $8,300mm of deal payments in operating cash flow, capital allocation whose assets the book values separately; $572mm of legal settlements; $1,200mm of US transition tax (2025 instalment 1,200mm). new_note: Case for lower: PARAGON-HF's echocardiographic study, on the same core laboratory and formula, found LV hypertrophy in 21% of 1,097 patients with preserved ejection fraction (Shah AM et al., J Am Coll Cardiol 2019;74(23):2858-2873, doi:10.1016/j.jacc.2019.09.063, PMID 31806129, PMC13537700); the same paper puts it at 42% to 75% in community cohorts and about 60% in hospital registries, which brackets 52%. Not applied, for want of a label that would carry them: NYHA class II to III with weekly diuretics (87% and 88% of the reduced and preserved outpatients above), NT-proBNP of 300 pg/mL or more, and the exclusions of eGFR below 30 and, in the preserved trial, implanted devices. Case for higher: the preserved trial also accepts a septal thickness of 1.1 cm in women or 1.2 cm in men, a looser test than LV mass
new_source: Both Phase 2s require LV hypertrophy on echocardiography (NCT06979362, NCT06979375: among the criteria, LV mass index above 115 g/m2 in men or 95 g/m2 in women on the linear formula), and the reduced ejection fraction trial also admits LV dilatation. LV hypertrophy on exactly that threshold was present in 52% of the TOPCAT echocardiographic study (456 of the 875 of its 935 heart failure patients with a measurable LV mass index), 43% concentric and 9% eccentric, read by a core laboratory, 52% of them enrolled in the US (Shah AM et al., Circ Heart Fail 2014;7(1):104-115, doi:10.1161/CIRCHEARTFAILURE.113.000887, PMID 24249049, PMC4467731). Applied to the whole pool, both ejection fraction halves: for the reduced half it is a floor, because LV mass index runs higher in reduced than in preserved ejection fraction (118 against 98 g/m2 among 831 consecutive heart failure outpatients, ESC Heart Fail 2021, doi:10.1002/ehf2.13366, PMID 34085774, PMC8318400) and that trial also admits dilatation without hypertrophy. 0.52 x 7.4mm = about 3.85mm

new_note: Judgement on the midpoint, since the paper's abstract gives the two extreme quartiles and not the total. Two ARTEMIS criteria are not applied because no source for their share was found: symptom onset within 12 hours (STEMI) or 24 hours (NSTEMI) before admission, and at least one risk enhancer (prior heart attack, prior revascularisation, treated diabetes, CKD, prior ischaemic stroke, carotid or peripheral artery disease, multivessel disease, or an anterior STEMI). Both cut the pool, so 0.4762 is an upper bound on them. The case for lower: the sample counts admissions, so transfers are counted twice, and admissions have fallen since 2004 to 2014. The case for higher: a label may read 'adults with acute MI' without the angiography condition
new_source: Two filters. (1) Hospitalised: 6,603,709 US AMI hospitalisations over 2004 to 2014 in the National Inpatient Sample (Matetic A et al., Am J Cardiol 2020;129:10-18, doi:10.1016/j.amjcard.2020.05.025, PMID 32576369), 600,337 a year, 0.7458 of the CDC's 805,000. (2) Type 1 heart attack confirmed by invasive angiography, an ARTEMIS entry criterion (registry): coronary angiography in 63.4% of the lowest income quartile and 64.3% of the highest (same paper); the midpoint 0.6385 is used. 0.7458 x 0.6385 = 0.4762, about 383,000 patients a year

new_note: Judgement: a multiple of 1.0 on the updated PCSK9 rate. Scaling by beneficiaries treats growth in the class's Medicare stock as growth in post-heart-attack starts; with about half stopping each year the stock settles in two to three years, so its growth mostly reflects starts. 2024 and 2025 include the Part D redesign, which is permanent and applies to a 2029 launch too. Optum CDM mixes commercial and Medicare Advantage, so MarketScan is taken as the commercial rate; at the CDM and MarketScan average the anchor is 0.4557% and the peak 1.93%. No independent forecast covers this indication: GlobalData's $148mm US by 2038 (pharmaceutical-technology.com, December 2024) predates ZEUS and covers CKD, ASCVD and heart failure, and the $3bn consensus quoted before ZEUS is withdrawn by the trial's failure. The case for higher: the drug would be started in hospital at the index event with no LDL threshold to meet. The case for lower: ZEUS showed no MACE benefit despite full IL-6 suppression, so cardiologists may doubt an anti-inflammatory even after a positive ARTEMIS, and payers will meet a biologic in an 800,000-a-year population with the restrictions they put on PCSK9s

new_source: ANCHOR, the capture_anchor identity (untreated pool, no opening stock, latest quarter x4) applied to Cobenfy, as abbv_emraclidine.csv measures it and rechecked here. US net revenue: $10mm in 2024 and $155mm in 2025 (BMY 10-K 0000014272-26-000004, where non-US is nil), and $240mm for 2026 (Q2 US $60mm x4, 8-K exhibit 0000014272-26-000018). Net per patient = 0.5 x $6,986.06 = $3,493.03. Stock: 2,863, 44,374 and 68,708. At this file's 59.26% stopping, 40.74% remain, so new starts are 2,863, 43,208 = 44,374 - 2,863 x 0.4074, and 50,632 = 68,708 - 44,374 x 0.4074. The pool is 1,200,448 less cumulative starts: 1,197,585 in 2025 and 1,154,377 in 2026. Capture: 3.608% in 2025 and 4.386% in 2026, which is the anchor. CROSS-CHECK: the revenue basis counts 3.95 Cobenfy patients per 2025 Part D beneficiary (44,374 against 11,246), which is where the convention may overstate the patient count. MULTIPLE 0.4, A JUDGEMENT: 0.4 x 4.386% = 1.754% of the untreated pool, the multiple the book puts on emraclidine, the other muscarinic entrant that would launch about nine years after Cobenfy. For more: Novartis lists GXV813 as an M4 agonist, where Cobenfy pairs xanomeline, 'a M1/M4 muscarinic agonist', with trospium, 'a peripheral muscarinic antagonist' (BMY 10-K), and Novartis has the scale to sell it. Against: STAR-1 is the first test of efficacy and has not read out; M4 selectivity has not yet been proven in a trial, since emraclidine's two Phase 2 EMPOWER trials missed their primary endpoint (AbbVie 10-K 0001551152-26-000008); and Cobenfy's combination patents expire in 2030, or 2033 if a pending term restoration is granted (BMY 10-K), so the class may carry a generic by the time GXV813 sells

Maciel G et al., Arthritis Care Res 2017;69:1612-1616 (doi 10.1002/acr.23173, PMC5478481), Olmsted County prevalent cohort on 1 Jan 2015: 9 of 106 with moderate (ESSDAI 5-13) and 7 with high (≥14) systemic activity, so 16/106 = 15.09% meet the ESSDAI ≥5 bar NEPTUNUS-1 and -2 enrolled. This is a floor. The authors warn that retrospective chart scoring under-counts the biological domain. The same group's incident cohort had 29.5% (18/61) at diagnosis (Maciel, Mayo Clin Proc 2017). NEPTUNUS also required diagnosis within 7.5 years and anti-Ro/SSA positivity, which the label may or may not carry. It MUST equal dazodalibep's value exactly: pool_crowding pools only claimants with the same prevalence x eligible_pct.

Capture identity from backend/capture_anchor.py (untreated convention), applied to Saphnelo, the last new biologic mechanism launched into a systemic autoimmune rheumatic disease. Saphnelo US revenue was $8m, $111m, $260m, $425m and $596m in 2021 to 2025 (AZ 20-F 0001104659-24-025553 and 0001104659-26-019130). The net price is $35,856 per patient-year (CMS Part B 2025: $38,007.17 per beneficiary x 1/1.06). That gives treated stocks of 223, 3,096, 7,251, 11,853 and 16,622. After 45.54% stop each year, new starts are 2,974, 5,565, 7,904 and 10,167. Against the untreated CDC SLE pool of 204,295, that is 1.46%, 2.77%, 4.04% and 5.42% (5.04% under the engine pool convention). 2025 is Saphnelo's fourth full year, which is 51.9% of the way up the fitted curve (k 0.31, midpoint 2.76). So the engine needs 10.45% to reproduce 5.42% at the same point. JUDGEMENT: multiple 0.75, giving 0.0784, which converts 4.07% of the untreated eligible pool in ianalumab's fourth year. Case for a higher multiple: it would be the first and only targeted Sjögren's therapy, while Saphnelo launched beside Benlysta. It is a monthly self-injection, not an IV. Two Phase 3s were positive and it has Breakthrough designation. The anchor is measured against all diagnosed SLE patients, not Saphnelo's narrower label pool, so it leans low. Case against: the placebo-adjusted ESSDAI gain was only -1.3 (NEPTUNUS-1, p=0.0496) and -1.0 (NEPTUNUS-2 monthly, p=0.041). The every-3-months arm failed (-0.5, p=0.34), and pooled patient-reported secondaries missed significance. ESSDAI must be scored for payers, and Maciel 2017 found community rheumatologists rarely run those tests. Crowded pool: dazodalibep follows in 2029, and nipocalimab (JNJ), deucravacitinib (BMY), telitacicept (VOR) and efgartigimod (argenx, readout July 2027) all have Sjögren's Phase 3s. None of them carries rows on indication 85 today. Pool crowding: pool_crowding.solve on indication:85 with dazodalibep rations no year (combined starts peak at 11.7% of the eligible pool). Counting the population once trims ianalumab's peak starts to 0.9348 of its standalone run.

new_source: Least-squares logistic fitted to Saphnelo's CMS Medicare new starts, 2022 to 2025 (index 0 = 2022, its first full year). New starts are Part B plus Part D beneficiaries (955, 1,670, 2,294, 2,875) net of the prior year's stock times 54.46% persistence: 935, 1,150, 1,385 and 1,626. The fit is k=0.31, midpoint 2.76, rmse 0.4. That is 4 points for 3 parameters, so one degree of freedom, and the rmse flatters it. It agrees with data/launch_ramp.csv, whose median launch peaks at 9 years: this curve reaches 90% of peak at year 9.9. Alternatives: a fit to the beneficiary stock gives k 0.82, midpoint 1.16, rmse 27.2. The book's Zeposia curve is k 1.005, midpoint 2.15.

new_note: The case for more: Pluvicto is also taken later, 23 of 89 third-line starts (25.8%) in the 2024 cohort, and across all lines of the 2021 to 2025 cohorts Lu-177 was started 723 times (113, 187, 215, 137 and 71 from first to fifth line) against about 2,600 men who reached a line after an ARPI (705 ARPI-experienced at first line, plus 3,541 ARPI-naive men started on an ARPI of whom the cohort's 53.6% reached a second line), roughly 28%; Pluvicto's pre-taxane label (efficacy supplement approved 2025-03-28, NDA215833) postdates most of that follow-up. The case for less: an add-on reaches only part of its partner's patients, the combination must beat Pluvicto alone (primary endpoint PSA50), Pluvicto's label now carries PSMA-positive hormone-sensitive disease in combination with an ARPI (efficacy supplement 37 approved 2026-07-31, NDA215833, openFDA; label effective 2026-08-12), which moves some of its use out of this line, and opevesostat, ifinatamab deruxtecan and JNJ-101556143 claim the same pool
new_source: ANCHOR, a measured share of the line. JSB462's lead use is added to Pluvicto (NCT07047118), so the patients it can reach are the ones who take Pluvicto. Among US mCRPC patients who started first-line therapy in 2024 (Flatiron, about 280 mostly community centres), Lu-177 was 47 of 344 second-line starts, 13.7% (Hooper et al., JAMA Netw Open 2026;9(6):e2620750, doi:10.1001/jamanetworkopen.2026.20750, PMC13316606), up from 18 of 894 (2.0%) in the 2021 cohort. Second line is the first line after an ARPI for most of the pool: 4,041 of 5,096 first lines (79.3%) across the 2021 to 2025 cohorts were an ARPI. So the base case gives JSB462 every Pluvicto patient in the line it is tested in. No independent peak forecast for JSB462 or ARV-766 was found: Novartis and Arvinas give none, and a search of analyst coverage found none

new_note: amortisation of acquired intangibles, restructuring and capital spending, none of which the filed expense lines carry, restated onto total revenue from the net sales base
new_source: derived and found to be nil: NVS's filed expense lines already leave less than the 31.44% of revenue it turned into free cash over 2023 to 2025, so there is nothing left to charge. Restated before interest: NVS paid $2,587mm of interest inside operating cash flow over 2023 to 2025, 1.72% of revenue. The free cash flow above is struck after it and the valuation already charges the debt by subtracting net debt, so adding it back only widens a gap the filed lines already leave, and the charge stays nil. Checked at replacement capex: no plant depreciation on file for every year, and no amortisation line to take it out of the combined figure, so the charge stands. Checked without one-off cash: deal payments are booked under investing, so free cash flow never carried them, and no settlement or transition tax is stated for the window, so the charge stands. Restated to the amortisation floor: the filed cost lines leave a 30.05% pre-tax margin where the cash over 2023 to 2025 supports 37.20%, so the charge rebuilds at -7.15%. It was held at nil, but NVS books $3,197mm of non-cash amortisation of acquired intangibles inside its cost lines in FY2025 (0001114448-26-000004), 5.86% of revenue, so the charge stops at that floor: -5.86%. Restated without working capital build: over 2023 to 2025 NVS's cash flow statement shows receivables up $3,559mm, inventories up $737mm, payables up $101mm, a working capital build of $4,195mm, 2.79% of revenue. Growth ties that cash up once, not on every product for ever, so the charge was held at the amortisation floor, -5.86% where the filed figures rebuild it at -7.15%, and stays there. Struck on total revenue: Novartis's filed cost lines sit against net sales of USD 54,532mm and other revenues of USD 2,142mm together (FY2025 20-F 0001114448-26-000004, Note 4), and the income statement shows other revenues above cost of goods sold with no cost of their own, so each ratio is scaled by 54,532 over 56,674 and charged on every revenue the model carries. The book's costs are the filed ones either way; this shares them across the revenue that earned them. Rebuilt on the book's own ratios on 0.3269 of the revenue they are struck on, against 0.3911 the filings leave as cash over 2023 to 2025 (free cash flow before interest, at replacement capex, without one-off cash and without working capital build), so the charge is -5.8626%.

new_source: uncomplicated cases, the triple's indication: 'Of the 1,059 patients with uncomplicated P. falciparum infections, 700 (66.1%) were hospitalized', against 1,273 P. falciparum cases in all (Malaria Surveillance, United States, 2018, MMWR Surveill Summ 2022;71(SS-8)); 1,059 / 1,273 = 0.8319. The rest are severe: 214 of the 251 severe cases were P. falciparum

new_note: the most arguable figure here. Against: GanLum (KLU156), Novartis's own non-artemisinin combination, positive in Phase 3 and due for submission in 2026, would reach the same patients first; generic atovaquone-proguanil takes six in ten US courses; artemisinin partial resistance is an African problem that rarely changes a US traveller's treatment; and two thirds of these patients are treated in hospital, where a single-dose cure saves little. For more: a single-dose cure active against resistant parasites, and the 16.4% share counts all species, where chloroquine (7.0%) serves only the non-falciparum cases
new_source: ANCHOR, a measured analogue: the share of US uncomplicated malaria treated with Coartem, the first and only artemisinin combination approved in the US (April 2009). In 2018, 'artemether-lumefantrine for 213 (16.4%)' of 1,296 patients with medications recorded, behind atovaquone-proguanil at 789 (60.9%) (Malaria Surveillance, United States, 2018, MMWR Surveill Summ 2022;71(SS-8)); in 2017, 200 (12.8%) of 1,567 (Malaria Surveillance, United States, 2017, MMWR Surveill Summ 2021;70(SS-2)), so it was still climbing nine years after approval. MULTIPLE 0.5, A JUDGEMENT: 0.5 x 16.4% = 8.2%

new_source: Two factors multiplied. new_source: The comparator is Voyxact (sibeprenlimab), Otsuka's anti-APRIL antibody for IgAN, approved 25 November 2025. It is self-injected every 4 weeks (openFDA label, effective 2026-03-17: 400 mg once every 4 weeks, one single-dose syringe per carton), so it matches zigakibart on class, disease and care setting. The source is CMS Medicare Quarterly Part D Spending by Drug (dataset 4ff7c618-4e40-483a-b390-c8a58c94fa15), 2026 Q1, still the latest quarter carrying Voyxact: $4,640,340.95 over 151 claims is $30,730.73 a claim, and 13 four-week doses a year gives $399,499.49. This uses the launch-year exception, not the per-beneficiary default. Voyxact's Q1 2026 per-beneficiary figure is $51,559.34: its 90 beneficiaries took 1.68 claims each, out of a 13-dose year, so that figure is a part-year artefact and not a price. It is the same class price povetacicept carries, and sefaxersen carries it converted to CHF. Alternatives: the published WAC of about $390,000 a year (ICER, B-Cell Directed Therapies for IgAN, 2026), which the per-claim figure sits 2.4% above; Trutakna (atacicept) at about $425,000 per the povetacicept seed (not re-verified here); Fabhalta at a 2026 Q1 Part D $47,568.79 a claim (monthly fill), about $570,800 a year, as the upside case. Zigakibart doses every 2 weeks (600 mg SC, per BEYOND), but the price is a class price per patient-year, so its dose count does not multiply it.

new_note: the 0.5 multiple is a judgement; pool_crowding keeps zigakibart at 92.6% of its uncrowded peak beside povetacicept and sefaxersen
new_source: This is the Filspari anchor times 0.5, and the 0.5 is a labelled judgement. I reproduced the capture_anchor identity myself. Filspari US net sales were $29.208mm (2023), $132.222mm (2024) and $322.005mm (2025), from Travere 8-K exhibits 99.1, 0001438533-25-000008 and 0001438533-26-000013. Its CMS Part D 2025 Q1-Q4 figure is $61,544,556.93 over 4,761 claims, or $12,926.81 a 30-tablet claim, which is $157,276.19 a year. That makes stocks of 185.7, 840.7 and 2,047.4 patients. Net of 27.5% stopping each year, new starts are 185.7, 706.1 and 1,437.9. Over the untreated eligible pool (198,887 x 0.6851 = 136,257.5, less prior starts) that is a capture of 0.136%, 0.519% and 1.062% (1.026% on the engine's pool plus incidence). Run through the engine itself (forecast.derive_new_patients and treated_stock, midpoint 1.7, k 1.32), it needs a peak of 0.01617 to reach 2,047.4 patients in year 3. The engine path tracks 219, 828 and 2,047 against the filed 186, 841 and 2,047. That is the 0.0162 povetacicept carries. The 2,047 is a floor, because the stock is divided by a gross price. The multiple of 0.5 gives 0.0081, the same as sefaxersen. Case for going lower: zigakibart is the fourth B-cell entrant. It arrives about 3 years after Voyxact (Nov 2025) and about 2.5 years after Trutakna (Jul 2026) and povetacicept (PDUFA 30 Nov 2026). It doses twice as often as Voyxact and povetacicept. ICER issued an access and affordability alert at $292,500 net: only 6% of eligible patients fit its $821mm budget threshold. Novartis's own Fabhalta and Vanrafia treat the same patients. Case for going higher: Novartis already has a nephrology field force through Fabhalta and Vanrafia, and BEYOND's primary endpoint is eGFR at week 104, which could support full approval where its peers launched on accelerated approval. Cross-check, also a judgement: if the class runs at about 3x Filspari's pace (the povetacicept seed's reading of Voyxact's 90 Q1 2026 beneficiaries) and is split by the order-of-entry penalty of Urban et al., Management Science 1986 (share ratio of about entry order^-0.49), a fourth entrant gets 0.507/2.80 x 3 = 0.54x Filspari, close to the 0.5 chosen. Re-solved 2026-10-05 after untreated patients were given an exit (carryover P/(P+I)): the same target now needs 0.00853856, was 0.0081 (the anchor path, now at carryover 0.9661, solves to 0.0170771, was 0.0161748, times the multiple of 0.5).

new_source: This is the book's own fit to Tarpeyo, the first IgAN-specific launch, carried so that all three IgAN claimants share one curve. Tarpeyo's CMS Part D beneficiaries were 52 (2022), 247 (2023) and 468 (2024) in the annual file (7e0b4365-fd63-4a29-8f5e-e0ac9f66a81b), and 680 in 2025 Q1-Q4 in the quarterly file. The book fits k 1.32, midpoint 1.70, rmse 17. My independent least-squares refit gives k 1.36, midpoint 1.67, rmse 16.5, the same shape on a flat error surface. Filspari (112, 323, 660 over 2023 to 2025) fits k 1.30, midpoint 1.66, but three points for three parameters is exact, so it describes the curve rather than testing it. new_note: JUDGEMENT on the HER2 share: the bottom of the trial sponsor's own range; its midpoint, 70%, gives 0.0961. The base is first-line-treated patients, the same denominator as the Flatiron share in penetration_peak_pct, so the two multiply on one basis. Case against, lower: SGNDV-001 enrols only patients eligible for platinum chemotherapy, so a label that follows the trial would leave out platinum-ineligible patients. Case against, higher: the JMCP flow model predates EV+P, which may have raised the share of la/mUC patients who get first-line therapy. Upper-tract tumours sit in neither the 84,530 nor, necessarily, the 11,600
new_source: Two filters. (1) About 22,542 US patients a year are diagnosed with or progress to la/mUC, of whom 11,600 receive first-line therapy (Hepp et al., 'Epidemiology and treatment patterns for locally advanced or metastatic urothelial carcinoma: a systematic literature review and gap analysis', J Manag Care Spec Pharm 2021;27(2):240, doi:10.18553/jmcp.2020.20285, PMID 33355035); the figure the vepugratinib seed carries. (2) HER2 IHC 1+ or higher, the SGNDV-001 entry criterion: 'In UC, approximately 60% to 80% of patients have tumors that demonstrate HER2 expression' (Powles et al., SGNDV-001 design paper, Future Oncol 2025;21(21):2705, doi:10.1080/14796694.2025.2535280, PMID 40728126), taken at 60%. 11,600 x 0.60 = 6,960 a year, over the book's 84,530 = 0.08234

new_note: JUDGEMENT: half of what the incumbent measurably captured in its first full year. The eligible pool is first-line-treated patients, the same denominator as this share. SGNDV-001 compares against chemotherapy, not EV+P, and EV+P is already standard in HER2-expressing patients, so DV must take share from Pfizer's own Padcev. Case for lower: no head-to-head against EV+P; nivolumab plus gemcitabine-cisplatin, the other new first-line regimen, reached only 4 of 935 first-line starts (0.4%) from April 2023 to September 2024 (Sonpavde et al., J Clin Oncol 2025;43(16 suppl):e16556, Flatiron); Pfizer's $1.6bn 2025 impairment on updated long-range forecasts. Case for higher: RC48-C016 matched EV-302's OS (31.5 months both) with a PFS hazard ratio of 0.36 against 0.45, and EV+P reached 62% of first-line starts in 2025 in the Ozay series. Check: 0.255 x 84,530 x 0.082338 = 1,775 starts a year, a plateau of about 3,780 US patients at 47% stopping
new_source: Incumbent: enfortumab vedotin plus pembrolizumab (Padcev plus Keytruda). Flatiron Health Research Database (Ozay et al., ASCO GU 2026, 'Real-world use and effectiveness of first-line enfortumab vedotin with pembrolizumab in patients with advanced urothelial carcinoma in the US', reported by UroToday 2026-02-28): 420 of 821 first-line patients (51%) received EV+P in 2024, from 142 of 919 (15%) in 2023. 0.51 x 0.5 = 0.255
new_unit: share of each year's eligible patients starting

new_note: Reused from the book's HER2 ADC launch fit, the closest measured analogue for a HER2 ADC. new_source: derived: Pfizer generated $23,703mm of free cash flow on $185,759mm of revenue over 2023, 2024 and 2025, a 12.76% margin, against the 33.8% its cost of sales, SG&A and R&D leave. The 2021 and 2022 COVID years are excluded because a 36% margin on a vaccine windfall is not what this company earns. Restated before interest: PFE paid $8,181mm of interest inside operating cash flow over 2023 to 2025, 4.40% of revenue. The free cash flow above is struck after it and the valuation already charges the debt by subtracting net debt, so the charge falls by that much, from 22.18% to 17.77%. Checked at replacement capex: no plant depreciation on file for every year, and no amortisation line to take it out of the combined figure, so the charge stands. Restated without one-off cash: PFE's free cash flow over 2023 to 2025 carried $1,350mm of deal payments in operating cash flow, capital allocation whose assets the book values separately; $63mm of legal settlements; $4,400mm of US transition tax (2023 instalment 1,000mm; 2024 instalment 1,300mm; 2025 instalment 2,100mm). None recurs, so the charge falls from 17.77% to 14.52%. Restated without working capital build: over 2023 to 2025 PFE's cash flow statement shows receivables up $25mm, inventories up $1,462mm, payables down $1,792mm, a working capital build of $3,279mm, 1.77% of revenue. Growth ties that cash up once, not on every product for ever, so the charge falls from 14.52% to 12.66%.

new_source: derived: Pfizer generated $23,703mm of free cash flow on $185,759mm of revenue over 2023, 2024 and 2025, a 12.76% margin, against the 33.8% its cost of sales, SG&A and R&D leave. The 2021 and 2022 COVID years are excluded because a 36% margin on a vaccine windfall is not what this company earns. Restated before interest: PFE paid $8,181mm of interest inside operating cash flow over 2023 to 2025, 4.40% of revenue. The free cash flow above is struck after it and the valuation already charges the debt by subtracting net debt, so the charge falls by that much, from 22.18% to 17.77%. Checked at replacement capex: no plant depreciation on file for every year, and no amortisation line to take it out of the combined figure, so the charge stands. Restated without one-off cash: PFE's free cash flow over 2023 to 2025 carried $1,350mm of deal payments in operating cash flow, capital allocation whose assets the book values separately; $63mm of legal settlements; $4,400mm of US transition tax (2023 instalment 1,000mm; 2024 instalment 1,300mm; 2025 instalment 2,100mm). None recurs, so the charge falls from 17.77% to 14.52%. Restated without working capital build: over 2023 to 2025 PFE's cash flow statement shows receivables up $25mm, inventories up $1,462mm, payables down $1,792mm, a working capital build of $3,279mm, 1.77% of revenue. Growth ties that cash up once, not on every product for ever, so the charge falls from 14.52% to 12.66%.

new_note: Oxbryta's rate across all SCD patients, taken as the rate in this narrower and sicker pool rather than scaled up. Severe patients were treated more often (Newman: DMT users had more VOCs than non-users; Chang M et al., Br J Haematol 2025;207(3):1070-1075, found voxelotor use three times the claims rate at comprehensive centres), and osivelotor's Phase 1 raised haemoglobin in SCD patients by a mean 2.3 g/dL after five weeks at 50 mg and three at 100 mg a day (GBT release, 13 December 2021, 8-K exhibit 99.1, 0001171843-21-008476). Against that, Pfizer withdrew Oxbryta after an imbalance in VOCs and deaths and withdrew its US NDAs on 31 July 2026 (Q2 2026 10-Q), the FDA put osivelotor on partial hold, and Pfizer impaired $820mm of osivelotor IPR&D in 2025 on updated long-range commercial forecasts (FY2025 10-K). Nothing displaces an HbS inhibitor today; hydroxyurea is used by 24.3% (Newman 2021). For scale, GBT and Pfizer put Oxbryta, inclacumab and GBT601 together at more than $3bn of worldwide peak sales when Pfizer agreed to buy GBT (joint release, 8-K exhibit 99.1, 0000950157-22-000902); Oxbryta itself peaked at $328mm in 2023 (8-K exhibit 99, 0000078003-24-000017), and this seed builds about $25mm a year

(1) Polivy US 2025 net sales were CHF 688mm (Roche Finance Information Tool FY2025, asset_revenue_regions) x 1.205919 USD/CHF (ECB 2025 annual averages: 1.129983 USD and 0.937031 CHF per EUR) = $829.7mm. (2) A six-cycle course nets $110,435: 2025 Part B spend per claim of $19,510.12 x 6 = $117,061, divided by 1.06. One claim is one dose: in 2024, 1,616,227 mg over 10,844 claims = 149 mg, one 1.8 mg/kg dose. That gives 7,513 course-equivalents. (3) First-line share: Medicare claims were 3,924 in 2022, before the April 2023 first-line label, and 13,091 in 2025. If relapsed use held flat, first line is 70.0%, a lower bound. That gives 5,261 first-line starts. (4) Polivy is a course (d=1), so starts equal the stock. The pool is each year's eligible diagnoses, 19,046 x 0.62 = 11,809. Capture was 44.6% in 2025, Polivy's second full year, and on the fitted curve below (87.3% of peak at index 1) the peak is 51.1%. JUDGEMENT: a multiple of 0.25 gives 12.8%. Against: US entry around 2030 behind Pola-R-CHP, with Roche (glofitamab plus Pola-R-CHP) and AbbVie/Genmab (epcoritamab plus R-CHOP) running their own first-line CD20xCD3 Phase 3s. new_note: Judgement on the comparator. Vyvgart Hytrulo is the only non-immunoglobulin biologic labelled for CIDP in the US, the product a new CIDP biologic would be priced against. Only its subcutaneous presentation is taken: Vyvgart IV (J9332) carries no CIDP label, so summing it would dilute the price with gMG-only patients. Part B although Part D now holds more of its beneficiaries (3,074 at $294,522.77, companion 4ff7c618-4e40-483a-b390-c8a58c94fa15): the Part B figure rests on ASP, which is net of manufacturer discounts, and the two parts' gross spend per beneficiary sit within 2% of each other, which leaves little room for the deep rebate the Part D convention assumes. Case against: the extension's prefilled pen points to pharmacy dispensing; at the Part D figure and the 0.5 convention the net would be EUR 129,551. Hytrulo's beneficiaries mix gMG and CIDP, and VITALIZE's comparator is IVIg itself. The peak is solved to a published estimate, so the price sets the patient count, not the peak. Before verification this row carried the 2024 Part B figure, $167,216, a part launch year

new_note: Corrected on verification from 0.27, which took the 27 points of the whole cohort that stopped between steady state and one year as 27% of the 68% on IVIG at steady state, and ignored censoring. IVIG persistence stands in for riliprubart's because no persistence figure for a CIDP biologic was found. Case for lower: the second year alone reads 0.19, closer to the stable maintenance patients VITALIZE enrols. Case for higher: the first year alone reads 0.44, and a switch to a new mechanism after a failed refractory trial may see more early stopping; counting only the index product, as a unique drug would be, also stops faster
new_source: Anderson-Smits C et al., Neurology and Therapy 2023, PMID 37171778, doi:10.1007/s40120-023-00478-5, full text PMC10310601, Fig. 4 (3,975 US CIDP patients initiating IVIG, MarketScan 2008-2018), read at each 4-month mark from the steady-state dose as patients on any immunoglobulin (index IVIG, a different IVIG or other IG), with the discontinued and censored shares: 72, 51, 35, 27, 23, 20 and 12% on therapy; stops of 12, 11, 4, 3, 2 and 0 points; censored 8, 5, 3, 2, 1 and 8 points. Life table with half of each interval's censored removed from the risk set: one-year persistence 0.8235 x 0.7732 x 0.8806 = 0.5607, two-year 0.5607 x 0.8846 x 0.9111 = 0.4520. As a constant annual rate over the two years: 1 - sqrt(0.4520) = 0.3277

new_note: A single broker, the weakest kind of independent forecast; no aggregator figure for riliprubart was found. The build reaches EUR 255mm in 2033, the estimate's year, passes EUR 400mm in 2037 and peaks in 2041, the modality-default loss of exclusivity. Before verification this row was 0.0278 on a pool that grew every year, and with the 2027 start it gave EUR 610mm in 2039 on the 2024 price

new_source: derived: Vertex generated $12,074mm of free cash flow on $49,396mm of revenue over the five years to 2025, a 24.44% margin, against the 33.0% its cost of sales, SG&A and R&D leave. Five years rather than three because operating cash flow was negative $493mm in 2024 on the Alpine acquisition, which takes a three-year window to 17.5% and lets one deal set the rate. Solved so the modelled book reproduces the margin rather than taken off a single line. Restated before interest: VRTX paid $195mm of interest inside operating cash flow over 2021 to 2025, 0.39% of revenue. The free cash flow above is struck after it and the valuation already charges the debt by subtracting net debt, so the charge falls by that much, from 10.33% to 9.94%. Restated at replacement capex: VRTX spent $1,375mm on plant over 2021 to 2025 against $758mm of plant depreciation, 1.25% of revenue above what keeps the plant running. Taken at depreciation, the charge falls from 9.94% to 8.47%. Restated without one-off cash: VRTX's free cash flow over 2021 to 2025 carried $6,517mm of deal payments in operating cash flow, capital allocation whose assets the book values separately. None recurs, so the charge falls from 8.47% to 0.00%. Restated to the amortisation floor: the filed cost lines leave a 39.05% pre-tax margin where the cash over 2021 to 2025 supports 43.77%, so the charge rebuilds at -4.72%. It was held at nil, but VRTX books $20mm of non-cash amortisation of acquired intangibles inside cost of sales in FY2025 (0000875320-26-000056), 0.17% of revenue, so the charge stops at that floor: -0.17%. Restated without working capital build: over 2021 to 2025 VRTX's cash flow statement shows receivables up $1,164mm, inventories up $1,594mm, payables up $288mm, a working capital build of $2,470mm, 5.00% of revenue. Growth ties that cash up once, not on every product for ever, so the charge was held at the amortisation floor, -0.17% where the filed figures rebuild it at -4.72%, and stays there.
